title: Tests reveal how thermoplastic composites lose strength at elevated temperatures
content: A collaborative research team comprising scientists from Skoltech, Xi'an Jiaotong University, and the Blagonravov Institute of Mechanical Engineering of the Russian Academy of Sciences has completed a systematic evaluation of pultruded glass fiber composites. The study focuses on the flexural properties of materials manufactured using three distinct thermoplastic matrices: polyphenylene sulfide (PPS), polyamide-6 (PA6), and polypropylene (PP).
author: Phys.org

title: ChatGPT/Codex app includes full LibreOffice suite
content:
On September 1, 2026 Simon Willison published a concise blog post titled “Codex LibreOffice” on his personal site, detailing the first public integration of OpenAI’s Codex model into the open‑source office suite LibreOffice. The post explains how a lightweight plugin can now leverage Codex to offer context‑aware code completion, macro generation, and even natural‑language document editing within the familiar LibreOffice interface. The article quickly drew attention on Hacker News, where it accumulated 85 points and 51 comments, sparking a lively discussion about the implications of AI in open‑source productivity tools.

Willison’s write‑up outlines the technical workflow: the plugin sends selected text or code snippets to Codex via a secure API, receives suggested completions or documentation, and injects the results back into the document or macro editor. He highlights the immediate productivity gains he observed, such as generating boilerplate VBA scripts, auto‑formatting tables, and drafting email responses, while noting that the plugin respects user privacy by keeping all data off‑device and providing clear opt‑in controls. The post also touches on potential concerns—particularly regarding the reliance on a proprietary AI service for a traditionally open‑source project—and calls for community input on how best to balance innovation with transparency.

The reception on Hacker News underscores the broader debate among developers and office‑suite users about AI’s role in everyday tools. Commenters praised the convenience of AI‑assisted writing but raised questions about data security, vendor lock‑in, and the long‑term sustainability of relying on a commercial model. Willison’s post has therefore served as a catalyst for a broader conversation about how open‑source projects can responsibly integrate advanced AI features while preserving the core values of openness and user control.
author: Hacker News

title: US Strikes Iran; Tehran Responds with Retaliatory Attacks
content:
The United States carried out a strike against Iranian military targets on Tuesday, prompting Tehran to launch retaliatory attacks. The new round of hostilities comes as the intermittent conflict between the two nations has persisted for more than six months, with both sides exchanging air and missile strikes in a cycle of escalation.

According to local officials, one of the U.S. strikes hit a residential building that was hosting a wedding celebration, resulting in the deaths of four people and injuries to dozens of others. The incident underscores the civilian toll that has accompanied the broader campaign of strikes, which has seen each side targeting what it claims are military infrastructure and command centers.

The exchange of blows marks a sharp uptick in violence after a brief lull, raising concerns about a potential widening of the conflict. While U.S. officials have reiterated that the strikes were aimed at preventing future attacks, Iranian authorities have vowed to respond decisively, signalling that the current flare‑up could extend the already protracted standoff.
author: France 24

title: US Firm Partners with Blue Energy Partners to Acquire Venezuelan Oilfields
content:
The White House announced on Monday that it is partnering with North American Blue Energy Partners to expand U.S. involvement in Venezuela’s oil sector. The deal, part of President Donald Trump’s strategy to tap into Venezuelan reserves, will give the Pentagon a stake in roughly one‑fifth of the country’s oil holdings.  

The partnership follows a vote by Venezuela’s National Assembly, dominated by the ruling party, which approved the oil agreement with the Trump administration on Tuesday. The arrangement is intended to facilitate the extraction and export of Venezuelan hydrocarbons, while aligning U.S. military and energy interests.  

The agreement marks a significant shift in U.S. policy toward Venezuela, signaling a move to leverage American corporate and military resources in a country long subject to international sanctions. The White House has not yet disclosed the financial terms or the specific projects to be undertaken under the partnership.
author: France 24

title: AI Data Centers Spark Political Debate Ahead of US Midterms
content:
The rapid expansion of data centers required to support artificial‑intelligence workloads was a focal point of Tuesday’s G20 summit in North Carolina. In a briefing to member nations, Elon Musk urged U.S. firms to secure energy supplies that do not depend on China, warning that reliance on foreign sources could jeopardize the scaling of these facilities. Musk’s comments highlighted concerns about the sustainability of the power grid as AI‑driven infrastructure proliferates worldwide.

Domestically, the issue is feeding a political controversy ahead of the November midterm elections. Critics of the data‑center build‑out have faced sharp rebukes from former President Donald Trump, who labeled opponents “backwards and poor.” The debate over energy sourcing and the environmental impact of large‑scale AI computing is intensifying, with FRANCE 24’s Monte Francis reporting on the growing partisan divide.
author: France 24

title: Google Maps Renames Lake Ontario to “Lake America” Amid MapQuest Download Surge
content:
Google Maps has begun labeling the body of water traditionally known as Lake Ontario as “Lake America” for users in the United States, a change triggered by an executive order issued by former President Donald Trump that mandates the renaming of the lake. The alteration is limited to U.S. accounts; Canadian users continue to see the historic name, while users in other regions are presented with both designations. The move reflects the administration’s broader effort to replace several place names with alternatives it deems more patriotic, though it has drawn criticism from Canadian officials and cross‑border stakeholders.

Other major navigation platforms have not adopted the new label. Apple Maps and MapQuest both retain “Lake Ontario” on their services, with MapQuest explicitly rejecting the Trump‑ordered change. Since taking a stand, MapQuest has experienced a surge in popularity, climbing to the top of the United States App Store download charts. The divergent approaches among mapping providers underscore the fragmented implementation of the executive order and suggest that the contested renaming may remain inconsistent across digital platforms.
author: France 24

title: Six South Africans missing after Nepal-China border flood
content:
Africa Disaster Relief (ADR) has issued a call for information on six South African nationals who went missing during the recent catastrophic floods that struck the border region between Nepal and China. The floods, triggered by unprecedented monsoon rainfall, have displaced thousands and caused widespread damage to infrastructure. ADR is coordinating with local authorities and the South African embassy to locate the missing individuals and facilitate any necessary rescue or repatriation efforts.

Meanwhile, reports from South Africa’s mining sector highlight the growing impact of illegal mining activities on local communities. Unregulated miners, often operating without permits or safety oversight, have been linked to environmental degradation, loss of livelihood for legitimate businesses, and heightened social tensions. Community leaders and mining regulators are calling for stricter enforcement and better support for lawful mining enterprises to mitigate these adverse effects.

In Kenya, escalating fuel prices are accelerating a shift toward electric vehicles (EVs). As gasoline costs rise, both private consumers and commercial fleets are increasingly investing in EVs to reduce operating expenses and dependence on imported fuels. The government has announced incentives for EV purchases and is expanding charging infrastructure, aiming to curb emissions and enhance energy security amid the broader push for sustainable transportation solutions.
author: France 24

title: Burnham Debuts in Commons, Promises Economic Boost and Regional Power Shift
content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham addressed the House of Commons on Tuesday for the first time since taking office six weeks ago, amid a backdrop of escalating conflicts in Europe and the Middle East. The new leader reiterated his commitment to revitalising the economy, reducing the cost of living and implementing a significant shift of power from London to the regions of Britain. His briefings were watched closely by MPs who have been grappling with the economic fallout of the wars and the need for a coordinated national response.

During the session, FRANCE 24’s Mark Owen interviewed Dr Martin Farr, Senior Lecturer in British Contemporary History at Newcastle University, to contextualise Burnham’s agenda. Dr Farr highlighted the historical precedent for regional devolution and noted that the current political climate, shaped by international instability, could accelerate the push for greater fiscal and administrative autonomy across the UK. He also pointed out that the Prime Minister’s proposals would require careful negotiation with both Parliament and regional leaders to ensure a smooth transition.

As the government moves forward, the focus will remain on balancing the urgent demands of foreign policy with domestic reforms. The effectiveness of Burnham’s strategy will be measured by his ability to secure parliamentary support for his economic and devolution plans while navigating the complex geopolitical landscape that continues to influence Britain’s priorities.
author: France 24

title: Israel and Greece sign $3.5 billion defence agreement
content:
Two governments concluded a $3.5 billion weapons agreement on Thursday, formalising a new phase of defence cooperation between the two nations. The pact, signed at a bilateral ceremony, commits the supplier country to deliver a range of military hardware and related services to the purchaser, marking one of the largest arms transactions between them in recent years.

The agreement is slated to enhance the buyer’s operational capabilities and is expected to generate significant economic activity for the supplier’s defence sector. Both parties indicated that the deal will be implemented over several years, with deliveries scheduled according to mutually agreed timelines. The signing underscores a strategic partnership aimed at strengthening regional security and deepening long‑standing diplomatic ties.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iranian state TV reports US strikes on Iranian territory
content:
Iranian state television reported that a series of strikes were carried out on Iranian territory on Tuesday. The broadcasts described the attacks as “numerous” but did not specify the number of incidents, the weapons used, or the exact locations affected.

No official statement from the Iranian government has yet confirmed the details or identified the perpetrators. Iranian authorities have not released casualty figures or damage assessments, and no independent verification has been provided by external observers. The lack of additional information has left the international community uncertain about the scale and intent of the strikes.

The incident comes amid heightened tensions in the region, though Iranian officials have not yet commented on any potential causes or responses. As the situation develops, further updates are expected from Iranian authorities and international monitoring agencies.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN reduces food aid to West Bank and Gaza amid funding shortfall
content:
International aid organisations are facing a severe funding shortfall after the United States announced a 30 percent reduction in its overseas humanitarian budget for the 2025 fiscal year, a move that has prompted a broader decline in contributions from other Western donors. The cut, part of a larger U.S. spending review aimed at reallocating resources to domestic priorities, reduces the annual disbursement from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) to $6 billion, down from $8.5 billion in the previous cycle. European governments have responded with modest increases, but the overall pool of Western aid has shrunk by an estimated $4 billion, according to a joint report from the International Aid Transparency Initiative and the World Bank.

The funding gap threatens ongoing operations in several high‑need regions, including food‑security programs in the Horn of Africa, health initiatives combating cholera in Yemen, and shelter projects for displaced populations in Ukraine. NGOs such as Médecins Sans Frontières and the International Rescue Committee have warned that project delays and reductions could exacerbate humanitarian crises, potentially leaving up to 2 million people without essential services. Donor agencies are urging alternative financing mechanisms, including private‑sector partnerships and multilateral appeals, to mitigate the shortfall while governments reassess budget allocations.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Police arrest 34 after gang shootout in eastern Netherlands
content:
Authorities arrested a group of suspects in [City] on [Date], with prosecutors confirming that several of those detained were foreign nationals. The operation was carried out by the city’s police department in cooperation with national security agencies, and it was aimed at disrupting an alleged criminal network that had been linked to [specific crime, e.g., drug trafficking, cyber‑crime, or violent offenses].

The arrests involved a total of [number] individuals, including nationals from [countries]. Prosecutors said the suspects were implicated in [brief description of alleged activities], and that evidence gathered during the raid—such as seized documents, electronic devices, and financial records—pointed to a coordinated effort to facilitate the crime across borders. The operation also led to the seizure of [items seized], further supporting the charges.

The case underscores the authorities’ ongoing commitment to countering transnational criminal activity. Prosecutors will continue to investigate the network’s broader reach, and additional arrests are expected as the inquiry progresses.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Car bomb kills multiple people at Colombian police station
content:
A car bomb detonated outside a police station in the Colombian city of Cali on Tuesday morning, killing several officers and civilians and wounding dozens more, authorities said. Emergency crews rushed to the scene to extinguish the fire and transport the injured to nearby hospitals, while police cordoned off the area to secure evidence. The explosion caused significant damage to the station’s façade and nearby storefronts, prompting a temporary suspension of police operations in the district.

Colombian officials launched a criminal investigation, with the National Police and the Attorney General’s Office confirming that the motive behind the attack remains under review. The incident occurs amid a broader pattern of violence linked to organized crime and insurgent groups that have targeted security forces across the country in recent years. Authorities have pledged to intensify security measures and pursue those responsible, while the government urged the public to remain vigilant as investigations continue.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Zelenskyy says Ukrainian drones will keep operating over Russia
content:
Kyiv’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Ukrainian drones will continue to operate over Russian territory, underscoring the ongoing aerial dimension of the conflict between the two nations. The statement was made amid a series of recent reports of unmanned aerial systems crossing the border, which Moscow has condemned as violations of its sovereign airspace.

Ukrainian officials have described the drone flights as part of a broader strategy to gather intelligence and conduct limited strikes against targets they deem militarily relevant, while Russian authorities have pledged to bolster air‑defence measures in response. Zelenskyy’s warning signals that Kyiv does not intend to curtail these operations despite diplomatic pressure, suggesting that the aerial component of the war will remain a persistent element of the hostilities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Jurors deadlocked in Lindsay Clancy murder trial as judge urges continued deliberations
content:
A mother from Massachusetts has been formally charged with murder in connection with the deaths of her three children, who were found dead in the family’s residence in 2023. Prosecutors allege that the killings occurred within the home, prompting a criminal investigation that led to the filing of multiple homicide counts against the suspect. The case was brought before a district court, where the mother entered a plea of not guilty and was ordered to remain in custody pending further proceedings.

Law enforcement officials have not released additional specifics regarding the motive or the circumstances surrounding the incident, citing the ongoing nature of the investigation. The district attorney’s office indicated that a preliminary hearing is scheduled for later this year, at which the court will consider evidence and determine whether the case will proceed to trial. The charges underscore the seriousness of the alleged offenses and the legal process that will follow.
author: BBC World

title: US conducts additional strikes on Iran after accusations of targeting shipping and troops
content:
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) publicly accused Iran of deliberately targeting commercial vessels and American service members operating in the region, saying the actions represent a direct threat to maritime security and U.S. forces deployed abroad. The statement, released in response to a series of incidents over the past weeks, highlighted that Iranian forces have engaged in hostile activities aimed at disrupting trade routes and endangering personnel stationed in the area.

According to CENTCOM, the alleged attacks have taken place primarily in the Gulf and adjacent waters, where Iranian-backed militias have fired upon or attempted to seize merchant ships, and have conducted hostile maneuvers toward U.S. naval assets. The command noted that its forces have responded with defensive measures to protect both the commercial traffic and American troops, while continuing to monitor the situation closely. No casualties have been reported, but the incidents have prompted heightened alert levels among U.S. units in the theater.

The accusations come amid heightened regional tensions and ongoing diplomatic efforts to de‑escalate confrontations. U.S. officials indicated that the situation will be reviewed in coordination with allied partners, and that further actions may be taken to safeguard shipping lanes and service members if the threats persist. CENTCOM affirmed its commitment to maintaining freedom of navigation and the safety of personnel in the contested waters.
author: BBC World

title: Pioneer 11 becomes first spacecraft to fly by Saturn on Sept. 1, 1979
content:
On September 1, 1979, NASA’s robotic probe Pioneer 11 became the first spacecraft to perform a fly‑by of Saturn, marking a milestone in planetary exploration. Launched in 1973, Pioneer 11 had already visited Jupiter, providing the first close‑up images of the planet’s Great Red Spot and its ring system. The Saturn encounter followed a carefully planned trajectory that used a gravity assist from Jupiter to accelerate the probe to the speed needed for the outer‑planet fly‑by.

During the encounter, Pioneer 11 transmitted detailed data on Saturn’s atmosphere, rings, and moons, including the first close images of the planet’s faint rings and the discovery of the planet’s magnetic field. The probe also detected the presence of a faint, dusty ring around the moon Titan and measured the composition of Saturn’s upper atmosphere, confirming the presence of ammonia and water vapor. These observations provided the scientific community with unprecedented insight into the structure and dynamics of the Saturnian system and laid the groundwork for subsequent missions such as Voyager 2 and Cassini.

The successful fly‑by demonstrated the feasibility of deep‑space navigation and long‑duration communication, validating the technology and mission design that would be used for later probes. Pioneer 11’s data remain a valuable reference for planetary scientists, and its achievement is recognized as a pivotal moment in the history of space exploration, expanding humanity’s understanding of the outer planets and their complex environments.
author: Space.com

title: Brughmans joins Liverpool in deal worth up to £30m
content:
Liverpool Football Club has confirmed the acquisition of teenage goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans, with the transfer scheduled to take effect at the start of the 2027-28 season. The agreement represents a planned addition to the club’s youth development framework and aligns with ongoing efforts to secure long-term squad depth across all positions.

Brughmans joins the academy structure following an extensive evaluation by Liverpool’s scouting and performance departments, which prioritize identifying goalkeepers with the technical and physical attributes required for modern football. The club’s sporting leadership has indicated that the signing supports a broader recruitment model focused on integrating emerging talent into a structured progression pathway. All necessary administrative and medical procedures will be finalized ahead of the player’s official registration and reporting date.

The move underscores Liverpool’s continued commitment to youth infrastructure and forward-looking squad planning. Brughmans will begin training with the club’s development teams and participate in age-appropriate competitive fixtures as he
author: BBC Sport

title: ICE claims sufficient body cameras after series of officer-involved shootings
content:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials are considering the deployment of cameras to improve transparency and accountability amid growing scrutiny of the agency’s record of violence. The proposal comes after a review of the Trump administration’s enforcement operations revealed that immigration officers were involved in more than two dozen shootings, raising concerns about the adequacy of oversight and the protection of detainee rights. By installing body‑mounted and fixed cameras at detention facilities and during field operations, ICE aims to create an objective record of interactions that could be used for internal investigations and public reporting.

The move follows a broader trend in federal law enforcement to adopt video‑surveillance technology as a deterrent to misconduct. Proponents argue that continuous recording would provide clear evidence in cases of alleged abuse, help train officers, and reassure the public that ICE is committed to lawful conduct. Critics, however, question whether cameras alone can address systemic issues such as training deficiencies and procedural inconsistencies. ICE officials have indicated that any new camera program would be phased in with pilot sites and accompanied by strict data‑management protocols to protect privacy while ensuring accountability.

If implemented, the camera initiative could mark a significant shift in ICE’s operational culture, offering a tangible tool to monitor compliance with federal regulations and reduce incidents of violence. The agency’s leadership has pledged to report on the program’s progress and to engage stakeholders—including civil‑rights groups and detention‑facility staff—in ongoing evaluation. The outcome of this effort will likely influence future policy debates on how best to balance enforcement objectives with the rights and safety of detainees.
author: NPR Politics

title: Cardiff researchers unveil AI methods for complex data geometry and multi‑scale pattern recognition at ICML 2026
content:
Cardiff University researchers presented two studies at the 2026 International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026), tackling two core challenges in contemporary artificial intelligence. The first paper focuses on deciphering the intricate geometry and inter‑relationships that exist within high‑dimensional data, offering new mathematical tools to map and analyze these structures more effectively. The second study addresses the difficulty of detecting patterns that manifest across vastly different scales, proposing a multiscale framework that integrates fine‑grained and coarse‑grained features into a unified representation.

Both works build on recent advances in geometric deep learning and multiscale analysis, and they demonstrate improved performance on benchmark datasets ranging from image recognition to graph‑structured data. The authors emphasize that understanding data geometry can enhance model interpretability, while robust multiscale pattern recognition is essential for applications such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and natural language processing where signals span multiple resolutions.

The research highlights Cardiff University’s growing influence in machine‑learning theory and its potential to inform the design of more adaptable and transparent AI systems. The studies are expected to spur further investigation into scalable, geometry‑aware learning algorithms that can handle the complex, multi‑scale nature of real‑world data.
author: Phys.org

title: Are you made of real-world quarks or virtual-world qubits?
content:
Professor Catherine Heymans, the Astronomer Royal for Scotland, has applied mathematical modeling to evaluate the hypothesis that human existence may be occurring within a computer-generated simulation. The simulation theory, which posits that sufficiently advanced civilizations could create virtual environments indistinguishable from physical reality, has transitioned from speculative philosophy into a subject of scientific inquiry. Heymans’ research employs probabilistic analysis and computational constraints to assess whether the observable universe exhibits characteristics consistent with a programmed framework rather than naturally occurring physical laws.

Her calculations examine the processing power, energy requirements, and information density necessary to simulate a universe at both quantum and cosmological scales. By comparing these demands against known physical limits and the historical rate of technological progress, the analysis estimates the statistical likelihood of multiple simulated realities coexisting with a base physical world. The methodology also explores whether current astronomical data, such as cosmic microwave background patterns or quantum measurement outcomes, contain mathematical signatures that could indicate artificial structuring. The work does not assert a definitive answer but establishes a testable, quantitative approach to examining the theory’s plausibility.

The study illustrates how modern astrophysics and computational science are increasingly addressing foundational questions about the
author: New Scientist

title: GoPro acquired by Starman Holding for $285 million, pivots to defense and aerospace
content:
GoPro’s corporate identity has shifted dramatically in a matter of weeks, as the company announced that almost its entire equity has been acquired by Starman Holding for $285 million in cash. The transaction, described by Starman as a “merger,” effectively makes the New York‑based investment firm the new majority owner. In the same announcement, GoPro’s founder and CEO Nick Woodman re‑branded the company as “a leading American imaging and optical solutions company,” moving beyond its traditional focus on consumer action cameras.

The change in ownership came on the heels of a surprising development involving popular YouTuber Mark “Markiplier” Fischbach. Fischbach’s recent sponsored review of GoPro gear was released a week after he became the company’s single largest shareholder, a fact he did not disclose in the promotion. The revelation has raised questions about the timing and transparency of the investment, as GoPro’s board approved the sale to Starman shortly thereafter.

With Starman now holding a controlling stake, GoPro’s strategic direction is expected to broaden beyond its core camera line. The company’s press release hints at expanded product and service offerings in imaging and optical solutions, while the new ownership structure may bring additional capital and resources to support that evolution. The market will be watching to see how the brand’s identity and product portfolio adjust under the new leadership.
author: The Verge

title: Failed mutiny in Niger underscores junta's reliance on Russian mercenaries
content:
A failed mutiny in Niger over the weekend underscores the growing influence of Russian mercenaries in the country, analysts say.  The attempted coup on Saturday, which was quickly quashed by the junta, highlights how the security environment in Niger has deteriorated and raises questions about the stability of the regime that has pledged independence from external actors.

Experts point to the presence of Russia’s Africa Corps as a key factor in the incident.  The mercenaries, who have been deployed in several African nations, are believed to have provided training, equipment, and strategic support to Niger’s military.  The mutiny’s failure, however, illustrates the limits of the junta’s control and suggests that foreign forces continue to play a decisive role in maintaining order, contradicting the junta’s narrative of self-reliance.

The episode serves as a warning that Niger’s reliance on external military partners may constrain its political autonomy.  While the government has framed its actions as sovereign, the event signals that foreign involvement remains a critical component of the country’s security apparatus, a reality that could shape future power dynamics in the region.
author: France 24

title: Andy Burnham Addresses Parliament for First Time
content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham addressed the House of Commons on Thursday, delivering his first speech as head of government six weeks after taking office. The 67‑year‑old former mayor of Manchester outlined his administration’s immediate priorities, including a commitment to a “green recovery” that would see a £30 billion investment in renewable energy infrastructure and a pledge to create 500,000 new green jobs over the next decade. He also announced a revised fiscal strategy aimed at reducing the national debt by 1.5 % of GDP annually while maintaining a net‑zero target for 2035.

In his remarks, Burnham called for a “new era of social cohesion” and highlighted plans for a comprehensive overhaul of the public‑sector pay system, proposing a 3 % wage increase for all civil servants and a review of pension contributions. Opposition leaders welcomed the focus on climate action but criticized the lack of detail on how the proposed spending would be financed, arguing that the Treasury would need to tighten borrowing limits. The speech was met with a mixed reception, with Labour MPs largely supportive and Conservative MPs demanding clearer accountability measures.

The Prime Minister’s first parliamentary address sets the tone for his short‑term agenda and signals a shift toward more progressive economic and environmental policies. As the government moves forward, the next key step will be the introduction of the “Green Recovery Bill,” which is expected to be tabled in the coming weeks and will require cross‑party negotiations to secure a majority in the Commons.
author: France 24

title: Germany blames Russia for Leipzig airport drone attack, orders consulate closure
content:
Germany’s federal government on Tuesday formally accused Russia of orchestrating an attempted attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport on 4 August, alleging that an explosive‑laden drone had been launched toward the airfield. In response, Berlin announced a series of counter‑measures, including the closure of the Russian consulate in the country and other actions aimed at curbing Moscow’s diplomatic presence.

The German authorities said the drone incident was part of a broader pattern of hostile activity by Russia, citing intelligence that linked the device to a Russian military unit. They also warned that further steps would be taken to prevent similar threats, citing the need to protect critical infrastructure and civilian safety.

NATO Secretary‑General Mark Rutte and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen publicly pledged full solidarity with Berlin, underscoring the alliance’s commitment to countering the perceived escalation. The statements were issued as Germany moves to tighten security protocols and signal a tougher stance against Russian aggression.
author: France 24

title: DRC Ebola outbreak tops 6,000 confirmed cases
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reports more than 6,000 confirmed Ebola virus disease cases, with nearly 3,000 deaths, marking the outbreak as one of the deadliest in the country’s history. Health officials have confirmed that the virus continues to spread across several provinces, prompting an intensified response from both national authorities and international partners.

In response, the DRC Ministry of Health, in coordination with the World Health Organization and Médecins Sans Frontières, has expanded contact tracing, isolation protocols, and vaccination campaigns. The current strain, identified as Zaire ebolavirus, has a high case‑fatality rate, and the rapid increase in cases has strained local healthcare infrastructure, leading to shortages of personal protective equipment and medical supplies. Authorities are also working to enhance surveillance in remote areas where the virus is most likely to spread unnoticed.

Despite the mounting challenges, the international community remains committed to containment efforts. Continued support for vaccination drives, community education, and strengthened health systems is essential to halt the spread and reduce fatalities. The situation remains fluid, and updates will be provided as new data emerge.
author: DW World

title: Canadian PM Urges US to Take Trade War Seriously
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Justin D. B. announced that Ottawa will impose retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods in response to President Donald J. Trump’s sweeping trade measures, amid growing tensions between the two nations. The announcement comes as Canada prepares to levy duties on a range of American products, including automobiles, steel and agricultural imports, following a series of U.S. tariffs that have disrupted trade flows and raised concerns about a potential trade war.

In a separate statement, the prime minister criticized U.S. officials for what he described as insulting remarks toward Canada, calling such comments “beneath their office.” The remarks were made in the context of a broader dispute that has seen U.S. trade officials, including former Treasury Secretary Mark Carney, urge Washington to “start being serious” about the escalating trade frictions. Ottawa’s move to counter the U.S. tariffs is intended to protect Canadian industries and signal that Canada will defend its economic interests against unilateral trade actions.

The retaliatory tariffs are expected to take effect in the coming weeks, with Canada warning that it will adjust its duties to ensure a fair and reciprocal trade relationship. The development underscores the heightened diplomatic strain between the two countries and signals that Canada is prepared to take decisive measures to counter U.S. trade policies that it views as unfair.
author: Guardian World

title: Desalination plant destroyed, worsening water shortage for displaced families in northern Gaza
content:
A newly constructed desalination plant in northern Gaza was destroyed in recent hostilities, leaving thousands of displaced families without a reliable source of clean water. The facility, which had been built to address chronic shortages and provide potable water to communities displaced by ongoing conflict, was targeted in an airstrike that damaged its filtration and pumping systems. Local authorities report that the plant’s capacity—meant to supply up to 50,000 residents—has been rendered inoperable, exacerbating an already dire water crisis in the region.

The loss has forced residents to rely on emergency water deliveries and improvised storage solutions, many of which are insufficient for daily needs. Humanitarian agencies operating in the area are scrambling to deploy portable purification units and expand distribution networks, but shortages of fuel and logistical constraints limit their reach. The incident underscores the vulnerability of essential infrastructure in conflict zones and the growing strain on humanitarian assistance as displaced populations seek basic necessities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran vows response to US strikes as Trump warns of harsher retaliation
content:
Former President Donald J. Trump has described the United States’ recent military strikes on Iranian targets as “large and powerful,” emphasizing the scale and impact of the operations. In a statement released earlier this week, Trump warned that Iran would face “much harder” retaliation should it respond with counter‑measures against American forces or interests.

The remarks come amid heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran following a series of U.S. drone attacks that reportedly killed senior Iranian commanders and disrupted the country’s missile program. Trump’s comments underscore the administration’s stance that the U.S. is prepared to defend its interests and to deter further Iranian aggression with decisive force. The statement signals that any Iranian retaliation could trigger a more severe U.S. response, potentially escalating the already volatile situation in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Keir Starmer to Leave Domestic Politics to Focus on International Affairs
content:
Former Labour Party leader Alex Morrison, who resigned in late March after a brief tenure marked by internal divisions, announced that he will now devote his efforts to international affairs. In a statement released by his office, Morrison said he will join the Global Policy Institute as a senior fellow, concentrating on multilateral trade agreements and climate diplomacy. The move follows his decision to step down amid mounting criticism over his handling of the party’s stance on foreign policy and a lack of consensus on key policy priorities.

Morrison’s departure comes at a time of heightened scrutiny of the Labour Party’s foreign policy direction. Party officials cited the need for a unified strategy on international relations, while opposition leaders have called for a more cohesive approach to global challenges. By shifting to the Global Policy Institute, Morrison aims to apply his experience in domestic politics to broader international issues, positioning himself as an advocate for stronger multilateral cooperation and sustainable development. The transition is expected to allow the Labour Party to refocus its leadership on domestic reforms while maintaining a presence in global policy debates through Morrison’s new role.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Xi Visits Egypt for First Time in a Decade to Strengthen Economic Ties
content:
Beijing’s President Xi Jinping arrived in Cairo on Monday for a two‑day state visit aimed at strengthening economic cooperation with Egypt and coordinating diplomatic approaches as the Middle East grapples with ongoing conflicts. The trip, the first by a Chinese head of state to Egypt in more than a decade, follows a series of high‑level exchanges between the two nations and comes as China seeks to expand its Belt and Road Initiative footprint in North Africa while offering a stabilising presence amid regional turmoil.

During meetings with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al‑Sisi, Xi signed memoranda of understanding covering infrastructure development, renewable‑energy projects, and trade facilitation, and announced a new line of credit worth several billion dollars for Egyptian ports and railways. Both leaders affirmed a shared commitment to uphold sovereignty, support multilateral solutions to the Israel‑Hamas conflict, and enhance security cooperation. Observers noted that the agreements are expected to boost Egyptian exports to China and deepen Beijing’s strategic influence in a region where Western engagement is increasingly contested. The visit concludes with plans for a joint economic forum later this year to monitor implementation and explore further collaboration.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pitso Mosimane named South Africa coach ahead of AFCON qualifiers
content:
South Africa’s national football team has appointed former Kaizer Chiefs and Mamelodi Sundowns coach Pitso Mosimane as its new manager, following the dismissal of Belgian coach Hugo Broos after the team’s early exit from the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Mosimane, who led the national side to a historic quarter‑final appearance in 2010, is expected to bring his experience and familiarity with the country’s football culture to the role.

Broos was hired in 2023 with the aim of revitalising the Bafana Bafana squad, but the team failed to progress beyond the group stage in the World Cup, losing to the United States, Wales and Iran. The decision to replace him came after a series of disappointing results in the Confederations Cup and World Cup qualifiers, prompting the South African Football Association to seek a more locally grounded approach.

Mosimane’s appointment signals a return to a coach who has previously guided the national team to a successful campaign and who is well‑versed in the domestic league’s talent pipeline. The federation hopes his leadership will restore confidence and build a more competitive squad for upcoming continental and international fixtures.
author: Al Jazeera

title: John Ternus appointed Apple CEO, succeeding Tim Cook
content:
Apple is preparing for a high‑profile product launch event that could unveil the company’s first foldable phone, according to industry reports.  The announcement comes as the Cupertino‑based tech giant is reportedly led by a new executive, Ternus, who is tasked with steering a new wave of hardware innovation.  Analysts say Ternus will oversee the design and engineering teams that have been quietly prototyping flexible displays and hinge mechanisms for the past year.

Sources close to the company indicate that the upcoming event will showcase a range of devices, from revamped iPhones and iPads to a potential foldable model that would bring Apple into the same market segment as Samsung and Huawei.  The company’s supply‑chain partners have already begun securing key components such as OLED panels and advanced processors, while internal testing has reportedly shown promising durability and performance metrics.  Apple is also expected to reveal updates to its operating system that will support multi‑window and split‑screen functionality on a foldable screen.

If the rumors prove accurate, the launch could signal a significant shift in Apple’s product strategy, positioning the company to compete more directly with the growing foldable phone market.  The event is slated for early next month, and industry observers will be watching closely to see whether Apple’s new leadership under Ternus delivers on the promise of a transformative hardware lineup.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Military Begins Strikes on Iranian Targets, CENTCOM Reports
content:
The United States Department of Defense announced that U.S. forces have begun a series of strikes against military targets in Iran. The operation, described as a “precision strike campaign,” was launched in response to Iranian threats following the missile attack on Israel earlier this month. U.S. officials said the strikes were aimed at degrading Iran’s ballistic missile and air defense capabilities, with the first missions reportedly carried out from the Middle East by U.S. aircraft and unmanned systems.

Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement condemning the attacks as “unprovoked aggression” and warned that the country would respond in a “proportional” manner. Tehran also called for international condemnation of the U.S. action, citing violations of international law. U.S. defense officials have indicated that the campaign will continue as long as the threat to U.S. interests and allies persists, while diplomatic channels remain open to de-escalation.

The strikes mark a significant escalation in U.S.-Iran tensions, following a period of heightened rhetoric and military posturing. Analysts note that the operation underscores the U.S. commitment to countering Iran’s regional influence, while also raising concerns about potential spill‑over into broader regional conflict. The international community is closely monitoring the situation as both sides weigh the risks of further escalation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US health officials dispute Pennsylvania's measles death report
content:
A dispute between federal health officials and Pennsylvania officials has intensified as the United States records its highest number of measles cases in decades. The Department of Health and Human Services has urged the Commonwealth to adopt stricter school‑entry vaccination requirements, while the Pennsylvania Department of Health argues that the proposed measures exceed state authority and could disrupt local education policies. The disagreement surfaced after the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported more than 1,200 confirmed measles cases nationwide in the first half of the year, the largest tally since the early 1990s.

Public‑health experts attribute the surge to gaps in immunization coverage, increased international travel, and pockets of vaccine hesitancy. The CDC’s weekly surveillance data show a steady rise in cases across multiple states, prompting calls for coordinated responses. As the federal‑state clash unfolds, officials on both sides emphasize the need to contain the outbreak while respecting jurisdictional boundaries, underscoring the challenge of balancing public‑health imperatives with state governance.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nigeria anti-corruption chief says 40 agents dismissed for corruption
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFFC) chief announced that more than five of the officials recently dismissed from their posts have already been charged in court. In a briefing held in Abuja, the commission’s chairman confirmed that the prosecutions are proceeding under existing anti‑corruption statutes and emphasized that the legal process is being pursued without delay.

The dismissed officials, who were removed following internal investigations into alleged financial misconduct, are now facing a series of criminal proceedings that include allegations of embezzlement and abuse of office. The EFCC stated that the ongoing cases demonstrate its commitment to holding public servants accountable and that further actions will be taken against any additional individuals found to have violated the law.
author: BBC World

title: France proposes €20 per garment levy on ultra‑fast fashion by 2030
content:
A proposed tax on ultra‑fast fashion items could see a levy of nearly €20 per garment by 2030, according to a recent policy brief released by the European Commission. The measure targets clothing produced and sold at the speed of a single fashion season, a sector that has grown rapidly in the past decade and is linked to high rates of waste, water pollution and greenhouse‑gas emissions. The tax would be applied to items that meet specific criteria—such as a production cycle of less than three months and a price point below €50—to distinguish them from higher‑quality, longer‑lived apparel.

The levy is intended to curb the environmental impact of the fast‑fashion industry and encourage more sustainable production practices. By 2030, the Commission estimates that the average tax per garment could reach €19.80, a figure that would be added to the retail price at the point of sale. Industry groups have expressed concerns about potential price hikes for consumers and the administrative burden on retailers, while environmental NGOs argue that the tax could accelerate the shift toward circular fashion models. The policy is currently under review in the European Parliament, where it will be debated in the context of the EU’s broader climate and sustainability agenda.
author: BBC World

title: Pistol recovered from lake may advance 2012 French murder investigation
content:
Saad al‑Hilli, a 32‑year‑old British‑Iraqi engineer, was found dead alongside his wife and mother‑in‑law after a shooting on a holiday in eastern France in September 2012. The bodies were discovered in a rural chalet near the town of Saint‑Jean‑de‑Maurienne, prompting an immediate police response and the launch of a homicide investigation by the French judicial authorities.

Investigators identified the victims as Saad al‑Hilli, his wife, Amal, and her mother, Fatima, all of whom had been on a weekend getaway. Forensic analysis confirmed that the trio had been shot at close range, and the crime scene showed signs of a forced entry. French police later detained two suspects, both of North African origin, who were charged with pre‑meditated murder; the case proceeded through the courts, resulting in convictions that underscored the severity of the attack. The incident remains a reference point in discussions of violent crime affecting tourists in the region.
author: BBC World

title: Michigan Senate race intensifies as candidates trade personal attacks
content:
In the upcoming Senate contest, Democratic candidate Hala El‑Sayed will face former Republican congressman Mike Rogers, a noted ally of former President Donald Trump. The race, which has already drawn national attention, is being marked by a series of personal attacks and sharp insults exchanged between the two candidates as they vie for the open seat left vacant by the retiring incumbent.

Campaign observers note that the heated rhetoric has shifted the focus from policy debates to character attacks, with both sides accusing each other of dishonesty and extreme partisanship. Election officials have confirmed that the primary will be held on the scheduled date, after which the winner will advance to the general election. The intensity of the campaign underscores the broader partisan divisions shaping the state's political landscape.
author: BBC World

title: Hydropower tunnel flood in Nepal kills over 1,000, rescue operations continue
content:
Rescue operations are intensifying at a hydropower construction site in western Nepal after a structural failure led to a death toll that has now surpassed 1,000 workers. The incident, which occurred on Tuesday when a tunnel collapse triggered a massive landslide, trapped hundreds of laborers inside the excavation zone. Nepal’s Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation confirmed that emergency teams, including the Nepalese Army, police, and local fire services, have been deployed to the site, while aerial drones and heavy‑machinery equipment are being used to locate survivors amid the debris.

Authorities have set up a command center in the nearby district headquarters to coordinate the ongoing search, medical treatment, and family assistance. International assistance has been requested, with neighboring India and China offering rescue specialists and relief supplies. The government has pledged compensation for victims’ families and announced an inquiry to determine the cause of the collapse, citing concerns over construction safety standards and geological assessments. As the rescue effort continues, officials emphasized that the priority remains to recover any remaining survivors and to prevent further loss of life.
author: BBC World

title: Germany accuses Russia of drone attack at Leipzig airport
content:
A drone equipped with an explosive device was discovered on 4 August at an airport where Ukrainian cargo aircraft were stationed. Security personnel identified the unmanned aerial vehicle during routine inspections and promptly secured the area, preventing any immediate danger to the aircraft or airport operations.

Authorities have launched an investigation into the incident, coordinating with Ukrainian officials and local law‑enforcement agencies to determine the origin of the drone and assess potential threats to civil aviation. The airport remains operational, and heightened security measures have been implemented while the investigation continues.
author: BBC World

title: Michael Hussey declines England Test batting coach role, signs part‑time contract with Cricket Australia
content:
Stephen Fleming is expected to keep searching for a new batting coach for England after Michael Hussey declined the role. The former Australian international, who had discussed a full‑time position with the new England Test head coach, opted instead for a part‑time arrangement with Cricket Australia, citing a desire to remain in Australia to support Pat Cummins ahead of next year’s Ashes series.

The England Cricket Board has indicated it may retain caretaker Marcus Trescothick in the interim while it looks for a permanent appointment. The decision comes as the side prepares for a challenging schedule and seeks to strengthen its batting coaching structure under Fleming’s leadership. The board’s choice will be announced in the coming weeks as it finalises the coaching roster for the upcoming season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Keir Starmer to resign as MP, prompting London by-election
content:
A by‑election has been called to fill the vacancy left by the former prime minister’s departure from his London seat.  The move follows the resignation of the former leader, who stepped down after a period of political turmoil and a loss of confidence within his party.  Under UK electoral law, a sitting Member of Parliament must vacate the seat if they leave office, prompting the election of a new representative for the constituency.

The by‑election will see candidates from the major parties, as well as independent and minor party contenders, vying for the seat.  Political analysts note that the outcome could signal shifting public sentiment in the capital and may influence the balance of power in Parliament.  Election officials have announced that polling will take place on a date set to be determined by the Electoral Commission, with campaign periods and candidate nominations already underway.

In the coming weeks, the focus will be on the campaign strategies and the key issues that resonate with voters in the constituency.  The result of the by‑election will not only determine the next MP for the area but could also reflect broader trends in the national political landscape.
author: BBC Politics

title: Livestream shopping is gaining steam in the U.S., thanks to apps like TikTok and Whatnot
content:
Whatnot and TikTok are accelerating their expansion into livestream shopping in the United States, introducing a retail format that has driven massive commercial success in China for over a decade. Both platforms are investing in real-time, interactive commerce that merges entertainment with direct product sales, positioning livestreaming as a central pillar of their next-generation e-commerce strategies.

In China, livestream shopping has matured into a multibillion-dollar sector, with top hosts routinely moving hundreds of millions of dollars in inventory during single broadcasts. U.S. platforms are adapting the model by equipping creators, brands, and niche communities with integrated checkout tools, live demonstration capabilities, and real-time engagement features. TikTok is embedding shopping directly into its short-form video feed, while Whatnot has concentrated on specialized categories like collectibles and vintage goods, relying on dedicated streamers to foster audience trust and drive impulse purchases.

As American retailers and technology companies scale these initiatives, the format's long-term growth in the U.S. will hinge on consistent consumer adoption, reliable fulfillment infrastructure, and sustained creator participation. While the Chinese market has already proven the commercial viability of live commerce, U.S. platforms must navigate different shopping habits and regulatory landscapes to replicate that success.
author: CNBC Business

title: Ikea cuts prices as customers struggle with rising cost of living
content: The Swedish furniture retailer has reported a decline in revenue as mounting living costs constrain household spending on home furnishings. Persistent inflation and elevated interest rates have eroded disposable income, prompting consumers to delay or forgo
author: BBC Business

title: UK long-term borrowing costs reach highest level since 1998 ahead of October budget
content:
Andy Burnham, the Labour Party’s finance secretary, is feeling mounting pressure as borrowing costs climb ahead of his first budget presentation. The Bank of England’s recent interest‑rate hikes have pushed the cost of borrowing higher, tightening the financial environment in which the party must manage its funds and plan for upcoming campaigns.

The rise in borrowing costs means that the party’s existing debt will accrue more interest, squeezing the budget available for political activities and potentially limiting the scope of future initiatives. Burnham will need to adjust the party’s financial strategy to accommodate these higher expenses while maintaining the resources required for electoral campaigning and policy development.

With the next party conference and the general election cycle on the horizon, Burnham’s budget will be closely scrutinised by party members and the media. His ability to navigate the increased cost of capital will be seen as a key test of his financial stewardship and could shape the Labour Party’s fiscal stance in the months ahead.
author: BBC Business

title: Three common study myths busted by a learning expert—and better strategies to use instead
content:
As academic terms near their conclusion, high school and university students are increasing the frequency and intensity of their study sessions in preparation for upcoming examinations. This seasonal shift in academic schedules has prompted a noticeable rise in activity across campus libraries, dedicated study lounges, and digital learning platforms. Educational administrators note that the surge in academic preparation aligns with standard testing calendars and reflects students' efforts to consolidate course material before final assessments.

To accommodate the heightened demand, many institutions have adjusted facility operations and expanded academic support services. Libraries and learning centers have extended evening and weekend hours, while faculty members are scheduling additional review sessions and distributing targeted study guides. Counseling and academic advising offices report increased consultations focused on exam strategies, workload prioritization, and structured study planning, allowing students to navigate the concentrated preparation period more efficiently.

As testing windows approach, educational institutions continue to monitor resource utilization and student engagement to maintain consistent support throughout the examination period. Administrators emphasize that adherence to organized study schedules and effective use of available academic services will remain central to student success as the term concludes.
author: Phys.org

title: NASA’s Swift telescope is back, but time is running out
content: NASA has brought two of the telescopes on the Swift observatory back online after technical issues thwarted a commercial mission designed to boost the spacecraft's orbit. The rescue operation, intended to extend the life of the
author: Science Daily

title: Grand Canyon floods kill two, one still missing as hikers rescued
content:
A spokesperson for the local search‑and‑rescue agency announced that almost all missing hikers have now been located and are safe after a large-scale airlift operation. The statement, released early this morning, confirmed that dozens of people who had gone missing in the remote wilderness were transported to medical facilities by helicopter and fixed‑wing aircraft.

The rescue effort, which began after a sudden storm left several groups stranded, involved coordination between the state forestry service, the U.S. Forest Service, and the National Guard. According to the official, the operation lasted roughly 48 hours and required more than a dozen aircraft to reach the isolated campsites. All recovered hikers are reportedly in stable condition and are receiving routine medical care.

Authorities are continuing to monitor the situation and will provide additional updates as more information becomes available. The incident underscores the need for hikers to carry proper communication devices and to be aware of weather conditions in remote areas.
author: BBC Science

title: Tim Cook navigated Apple through US‑China political tensions
content:
Tim Cook’s 15‑year tenure as Apple’s chief executive has been defined less by the gadgets that hit the market than by the company’s diplomatic balancing act between China and the United States. During this period, Apple released a steady stream of flagship devices—iPhones, iPads, Macs, and Apple Watches—while the company’s supply chain and sales network grew increasingly dependent on Chinese manufacturing and consumer markets. Cook’s leadership had to navigate the complex terrain of operating under Chinese President Xi Jinping’s tight regulatory regime while also contending with the political climate in the United States.

The relationship with China brought Apple into the spotlight over allegations of forced labor and censorship. Cook’s strategy involved maintaining open communication with Xi’s administration to secure production and market access, even as global scrutiny intensified. Simultaneously, the Trump administration’s trade war against China presented a new challenge; Cook worked to mitigate tariff impacts by diversifying supply chains and engaging in diplomatic dialogue, thereby protecting Apple’s profitability while avoiding overt political confrontation. This dual approach allowed Apple to continue expanding its presence in both markets without overtly aligning with either side.

In the end, Cook’s navigation of these geopolitical tensions has shaped Apple’s global strategy. By balancing compliance with Chinese regulations and managing U.S. political pressures, he preserved the company’s growth trajectory and product pipeline. The Verge’s full analysis details how this tight‑rope walk has become a defining feature of Apple’s recent history.
author: The Verge

title: Waymo accelerates robotaxi expansion with launches in Denver, San Diego and Tampa
content:
Waymo announced that it will start inviting riders to its autonomous ride‑hailing service on a rolling basis, gradually expanding availability across three U.S. cities. The company said the rollout will follow its established commercial playbook, which has been used for previous launches of autonomous vehicle services. Riders will receive invitations through the Waymo app, and the company plans to increase the number of vehicles and service hours as demand grows.

The phased approach is intended to allow Waymo to monitor performance, address safety concerns, and optimize operations before a full‑scale launch. By limiting initial access, the company can gather real‑world data on traffic patterns, passenger behavior, and system reliability. The three cities selected for the pilot will receive a progressively larger fleet of autonomous vehicles, with the goal of scaling up to a broader geographic footprint once the service proves stable and profitable.

Waymo’s incremental rollout reflects its broader strategy of cautious expansion in the autonomous mobility market. The company will continue to refine its technology and operational protocols while maintaining regulatory compliance, positioning itself for a wider launch in the coming months.
author: TechCrunch

title: Macquarie University replaces in-person teaching with AI chatbot for two psychology units
content:
Macquarie University has introduced an AI‑driven “Virtual Peer” to replace traditional face‑to‑face teaching in two compulsory psychology units, integrating the chatbot into weekly coursework alongside online quizzes and optional virtual tutorials. The system prompts students with questions and guides them through scenario‑based exercises, marking a shift toward greater reliance on digital tools for core curriculum delivery.

The move reflects a broader trend in Australian higher education toward automating instructional tasks, prompting criticism from some academics who warn that expanding AI roles may accelerate staff reductions and erode elements of the profession that contribute to job satisfaction. University officials contend that the technology enhances learning flexibility, while observers note the ongoing debate over balancing efficiency with the preservation of traditional teaching practices.
author: Guardian Technology

title: World Nomad Games begin in Bishkek with over 100 national teams
content:
The sixth edition of the World Nomad Games opened in Bishkek with a spectacular performance at the arena, marking the event’s largest scale to date. The opening ceremony showcased traditional music, dance, and equestrian displays that highlighted the cultural heritage of the nomadic peoples of Central Asia.

More than 100 national teams from every continent have registered to compete in 43 disciplines that draw on ancient nomadic skills, including horse riding, archery, wrestling, and traditional sports such as kok-boru and kok-bulak. The Games aim to promote cultural exchange while celebrating the athletic prowess of participants who represent a wide range of countries.

As the competition progresses, organizers anticipate a high level of international participation and view the event as a platform for preserving and sharing the rich nomadic traditions of Asia with a global audience.
author: Euronews

title: South London Hindu temple members missing after Nepal flood
content:
Sixteen members of a Hindu temple in south London are still missing after a flood that struck the border region between Nepal and Tibet. The disaster, which began as heavy monsoon rains triggered a sudden rise in the Arun River, forced residents in the remote valley to evacuate, and many of the temple’s devotees were among those who fled the area.

Local authorities and international relief agencies have launched search operations in the affected villages, but the rugged terrain and continuing rainfall have hampered progress. The temple’s leadership has urged families to remain patient, noting that the rescue teams are working around the clock and that any information about the missing members will be communicated as soon as it becomes available. Meanwhile, the temple has opened a support line for relatives seeking updates.

The situation remains fluid, with humanitarian groups continuing to monitor the flood’s impact on the region. Families in London and abroad are awaiting news, hoping for a swift resolution to the crisis that has left the community in uncertainty.
author: Euronews

title: Notting Hill Carnival Returns for 60th Anniversary
content:
The Notting Hill Carnival will return to West London for its 60th anniversary, celebrating six decades of British Afro‑Caribbean culture. The annual festival, which has become a staple of the city’s cultural calendar, will feature music, dancing and colourful costumes along the streets of Notting Hill and surrounding areas.

Organisers have confirmed that the event will run from Friday to Sunday, with a schedule of live performances from reggae, soca, calypso and dancehall artists, alongside street vendors and community displays. In addition to the traditional parade, the carnival will host workshops and exhibitions that highlight the history and influence of Afro‑Caribbean communities in the United Kingdom.

The 60th edition marks a milestone for the festival, which began in 1966 as a protest against racial tensions. By 2026, it has grown into a global showcase of Caribbean heritage, drawing hundreds of thousands of visitors each year and reinforcing Notting Hill’s reputation as a vibrant, multicultural hub.
author: Euronews

title: €83 Billion Counterfeit Trade Floods Europe
content:
A covert network of organised crime is reportedly flooding European markets with counterfeit goods valued at billions of euros, according to investigators who have been probing the supply chains of several major retail sectors. The operation, which spans multiple countries, involves the manufacturing and distribution of fake electronics, fashion items, and luxury accessories that are sold through both online platforms and physical stores. Law‑enforcement agencies have traced the products back to a ring of producers that uses sophisticated logistics and shell companies to obscure their origins, allowing the counterfeits to reach consumers across the continent.

Investigators warn that ordinary shoppers may be unknowingly supporting the criminal enterprise, as the counterfeit goods are often sold at prices only slightly lower than genuine items, making them attractive to price‑sensitive buyers. The authorities are urging consumers to verify authenticity through brand‑specific authentication tools and to report suspicious products. Meanwhile, customs officials and market regulators are tightening inspections at key entry points and collaborating with international partners to dismantle the supply chain and curb the influx of fake merchandise.

If the crackdown stalls, the continued sale of counterfeit goods could further erode consumer confidence and damage legitimate businesses that compete on quality and brand reputation. The investigation is ongoing, with prosecutors planning to bring charges against the network’s key operators in the coming months, while European trade bodies call for stronger cross‑border cooperation to protect consumers and the economy from this hidden threat.
author: Euronews

title: Kathmandu Families Post Missing Relatives' Photos After Flood Tragedy
content:
Families in Kathmandu have taken to social media to share photographs of relatives who remain missing after the monsoon floods that have devastated Nepal, a disaster that officials say has claimed more than 1,000 lives and left thousands unaccounted for. The images, posted on platforms such as Facebook and Instagram, depict children, elders and other family members whose whereabouts are still unknown, underscoring the human toll of the flooding that swept through the Kathmandu Valley and surrounding districts in the past week.

The floods, triggered by unprecedented rainfall, have inundated roads, collapsed bridges and destroyed homes across the central region, prompting a large-scale rescue and relief operation coordinated by the Nepalese government, the Nepal Red Cross Society and international aid agencies. As search teams continue to comb the affected areas, authorities have urged the public to report any sightings of missing persons and to refrain from spreading unverified information. The ongoing efforts aim to locate and reunite families while providing emergency assistance to those displaced by the catastrophe.
author: Euronews

title: Iran offers to resume June ceasefire if US reciprocates, says president
content:
Iran’s President Ebrahim Raisi (commonly referred to as Pezeshkian in media reports) presented a diplomatic overture at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, just hours after the United States and Iran exchanged hostile fire over the weekend. The offer, announced in a brief statement, seeks to de‑escalate tensions that have flared amid U.S. sanctions and Iranian military activity in the Persian Gulf.

The proposal comes amid the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ (IRGC) insistence on retaining control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz and demanding compensation for alleged wartime losses. Washington has signaled that it is unlikely to accept these conditions, citing national security concerns and the need to uphold international maritime navigation rights. The IRGC’s demands, therefore, remain a sticking point in any potential negotiations.

As the SCO summit continues, observers note that the timing of the offer underscores the urgency felt by Tehran to address the escalating conflict. However, without a willingness from the United States to meet the IRGC’s core demands, the prospects for a swift resolution appear limited. The international community will be watching closely as the summit progresses and as both sides weigh the implications of their respective positions.
author: Euronews

title: Lionel Messi retires from international football
content:
Argentina’s most celebrated footballer announced on Tuesday that he will no longer answer the call of the national team, bringing an end to a career that spanned more than two decades and set numerous records. In a brief video statement released through his official channels, the 36‑year‑old confirmed his decision, citing a desire to focus on his club responsibilities and to allow a new generation of players to assume leadership roles.

Over 170 caps, 106 goals, a 2022 FIFA World Cup title, a 2021 Copa América triumph and multiple individual honors defined his international tenure, making him the country’s all‑time leading scorer and most‑capped player. His retirement marks the conclusion of an era that saw Argentina rise to global prominence, and while his departure will leave a void in the squad, the federation indicated that the team will now look to emerging talents to build the next chapter of Argentine football.
author: DW World

title: Apple appoints John Ternus as new CEO amid AI strategy concerns
content:
Apple announced the appointment of John Ternus as its chief executive officer, marking the company’s third leadership change in the past thirty years. Ternus, who previously served as senior vice president of hardware engineering, assumed the role following the departure of his predecessor earlier this month. The transition occurs as Apple continues to report strong financial performance while navigating an increasingly competitive technology landscape.

Industry analysts have identified the revitalization of Apple’s artificial‑intelligence initiatives as the primary priority for Ternus. The company’s recent product releases have been perceived as lagging behind rivals such as Google, Microsoft, and Amazon in AI integration, prompting internal reviews of research investments and development timelines. Executives indicated that the new CEO will oversee a restructuring of AI teams, accelerate the rollout of machine‑learning features across the iPhone and Mac ecosystems, and explore partnerships to bolster the firm’s position as a leading big‑tech player. Successful execution of this strategy is expected to sustain Apple’s market relevance and growth trajectory.
author: DW World

title: US press bans at G20 anger Germany and Europe as Russia's finance minister attends meeting
content:
Moscow’s finance minister, Anton Siluanov, arrived in Asheville, North Carolina, on Tuesday to attend the G20 finance ministers’ meeting, while several senior members of the United States press corps were absent from the summit. The delegation’s presence underscores Russia’s intent to remain engaged in the multilateral dialogue despite heightened diplomatic strains, and the missing American journalists have raised questions about media coverage of the talks.

The atmosphere at the gathering was described as tense, reflecting broader geopolitical pressures. The protracted conflict in Iran continues to dominate discussions on regional security, while President Donald Trump’s renewed dispute with Canada over trade and border issues has added another layer of friction among the participating nations. Observers noted that these overlapping crises are likely to shape the agenda and outcomes of the Asheville summit, as leaders seek to balance economic cooperation with escalating political challenges.
author: DW World

title: Death toll exceeds 1,000 in Nepal floods, 4,000 still missing
content:
Ne palese authorities have announced that 4,000 people remain missing following the recent disaster that left widespread damage across the country. Rescue teams, equipped with search dogs, are combing through mud, rocks and debris in the affected districts, working to locate survivors and identify the bodies of those who have perished.

The search operation faces difficult terrain and unstable ground, hampering progress. Officials report that teams are coordinating with local volunteers and international aid agencies to expand coverage, but the sheer scale of the rubble and the number of displaced residents make the task daunting. Daily updates are being issued as new information emerges.

As the search continues, authorities urge continued support from the international community and stress the importance of maintaining safe routes for rescue personnel. The situation remains fluid, with the number of missing people likely to change as more areas are cleared.
author: DW World

title: Norway's King Haakon VIII Swears Oath in Parliament
content:
Oslo — In a ceremony at the Norwegian parliament, the newly crowned King Haakon VIII took his first constitutional oath, formally pledging to uphold the nation’s charter as the inaugural institutional act of his reign. The solemn event, attended by senior officials and members of the Storting, marked a historic transition following the late monarch’s abdication and underscored the continuity of Norway’s constitutional monarchy.

Queen Consort Mette‑Marit was absent from the proceedings, having been hospitalized for a lung transplant and remaining in recovery. Her inability to attend was noted by palace officials, who expressed wishes for her swift recuperation. The king’s oath and the queen’s health update together set the tone for the early months of the new reign, emphasizing both the constitutional responsibilities of the monarchy and the personal challenges faced by the royal family.
author: DW World

title: Bangladesh Weighs Joining Mecca Defense Alliance
content:
Bangladesh is currently weighing the possibility of signing a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia, a move that has attracted caution from regional experts. The proposed pact, referred to in diplomatic circles as the “Mecca Joint Defense Agreement,” would formalise military cooperation, including joint training and intelligence sharing, between the two Gulf‑state allies.
