author: Medical Xpress

title: Americans' confidence in personal health care providers stays high, survey shows
content:
Americans continue to express strong confidence in their health‑care providers, a finding that emerged from a longitudinal, nationally representative survey conducted by the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) of the University of Pennsylvania. The study tracked respondents from April 2021 through August 2026, capturing attitudes across five years of significant health‑policy changes and the ongoing COVID‑19 pandemic.

The APPC survey, which sampled thousands of adults across all states, consistently reported high levels of trust in physicians, nurses, and other health‑care professionals. While the data set did not show a statistically significant decline in confidence during the study period, it did reveal subtle shifts in specific subgroups, such as younger adults and those living in rural areas, who reported slightly lower trust scores compared with older, urban respondents. The researchers emphasized that the overall trend remained positive, suggesting that despite disruptions to health‑care delivery, the public’s faith in medical providers has largely persisted.

These findings underscore the resilience of patient‑provider relationships amid evolving health‑care landscapes. Policymakers and health‑care organizations can use the longitudinal evidence to guide strategies that maintain and strengthen public confidence, particularly in communities where trust has eroded. The APPC’s ongoing monitoring will continue to inform efforts to ensure that health‑care delivery remains both accessible and trusted across the United States.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Digital strategy helps patients with heart failure to receive proven medication
content:
A registry‑based digital strategy that identified patients with heart failure who had not received guideline‑directed therapy and invited them to a telephone consultation more than doubled the uptake of an effective treatment, according to data presented at the ESC Congress 2026. The findings were disclosed during a Hot Line session and stem from the EMAIL‑HF trial, which leveraged electronic health records to flag untreated individuals and automatically schedule remote clinical assessments.

The trial demonstrated that the proactive outreach model led to a rapid increase in prescription of the evidence‑based therapy, with implementation rates rising from roughly 30 % in standard care to over 70 % among participants who received the telephone consultation. Researchers highlighted the scalability of the approach, noting that digital registries combined with simple telephonic engagement can bridge treatment gaps in chronic cardiovascular disease without requiring extensive in‑person resources. The results suggest a viable pathway for health systems to improve guideline adherence and outcomes for heart‑failure patients worldwide.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Anthropic sued by music publishers over alleged use of tens of thousands of songs
content:
A lawsuit alleging the misuse of copyrighted music to train artificial‑intelligence models has been filed against Anthropic, the startup behind the Claude chatbot. Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell, two major music publishers representing songwriters and composers, claim that Anthropic used “tens of thousands” of copyrighted works without permission in the development of its language‑model technology. The plaintiffs are seeking multibillion‑dollar damages for the alleged infringement and for the unauthorized use of their catalogues.

The suit argues that the AI training process incorporated large amounts of copyrighted audio and lyrics, providing the models with proprietary content that was never licensed. Anthropic maintains that it complied with applicable copyright laws and that the data used were either public domain or properly licensed. The case highlights the growing legal scrutiny of how AI companies source and use copyrighted material during model training, raising questions about the balance between technological innovation and intellectual‑property rights.

If the court sides with Sony and Warner Chappell, the decision could set a precedent for how AI firms obtain and use copyrighted works, potentially reshaping licensing practices in the industry. The lawsuit remains pending, with both parties preparing for a protracted legal battle that could influence future AI‑training protocols.
author: Guardian Business

title: FTC and 22 states sue Amazon for alleged secret surcharges on advertisers
content:
The Federal Trade Commission, joined by 22 states, filed a lawsuit against Amazon on Monday alleging that the online retailer “secretly and systematically overcharged” advertisers for years. According to the complaint, Amazon’s alleged pricing practices inflated the cost of advertising on its platform, which in turn raised prices for consumers on essential goods such as groceries and other household items sold through the site. The plaintiffs argue that the higher advertising fees were passed on to buyers, creating a direct link between Amazon’s billing practices and increased consumer costs.

The lawsuit claims that Amazon’s overcharging was not an isolated incident but a deliberate, long‑term strategy to maximize revenue from advertisers. The FTC and the states seek to halt the alleged practices and recover damages, asserting that the company’s conduct violated antitrust and consumer protection laws. Amazon has not yet responded to the allegations. The case is expected to prompt a broader examination of how e‑commerce platforms price advertising and the impact on consumer prices.
author: Guardian Business

title: Trump urges Apple to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America on maps
content:
A request to rename a U.S. geographic feature has gained attention after Google implemented the change for its American users over the weekend. The alteration, which updates the name across Google Maps and related services, reflects a broader effort by the tech giant to align its mapping data with recent official decisions made by local authorities.

MapQuest, another major provider of online maps in the United States, announced that it will retain the original name in its database, citing a commitment to its existing data standards. The differing approaches highlight the lack of a uniform protocol among mapping platforms for incorporating newly approved place‑name changes, leaving users to encounter inconsistent labeling across services.
author: BBC Business

title: EU policy brief urges sponge landscape restoration to boost water resilience
content:
European water and climate resilience faces mounting challenges as degraded soils, drained catchments and the loss of wetlands amplify droughts and heighten flood risks. In response, three EU‑funded initiatives—SpongeBoost, SpongeWorks and SpongeScapes—have jointly released a policy brief titled *“Achieving Better Implementation of EU Policies by Restoring the Sponge Function.”* The brief outlines a set of recommendations aimed at strengthening Europe’s capacity to manage water by restoring the natural sponge function of landscapes, which enables soils, wetlands, forests and floodplains to absorb, store and slowly release water.

The brief combines policy guidance, scientific evidence and case studies from across Europe to illustrate how sponge landscapes can be integrated into existing EU frameworks. It calls for enhanced cross‑border cooperation, clearer regulatory incentives, and increased investment in nature‑based solutions that restore wetlands, re‑vegetate floodplains and protect forested catchments. By aligning national policies with the EU’s Green Deal and Water Framework Directive, the projects seek to accelerate the adoption of sponge landscapes as a cost‑effective, climate‑adaptation strategy.

In conclusion, the joint brief positions the restoration of the sponge function as a central pillar for future water and climate resilience in Europe. If implemented, the recommendations could reduce the severity of both droughts and floods, while delivering co‑benefits such as biodiversity conservation and improved water quality. The projects invite policymakers, stakeholders and local communities to collaborate in scaling up these nature‑based solutions across the continent.
author: Phys.org

title: Astronomy Picture of the Day Highlights Plane Lunar Eclipse, September 1 2026
content:
Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) released its September 1, 2026 entry today, continuing the long‑standing tradition of showcasing a new image of the cosmos each day. The featured photograph, titled “A Plane,” presents a striking view of a vast, flattened structure that astronomers have identified as a prominent galactic plane. The image was captured with a high‑resolution telescope and processed to highlight the distribution of interstellar dust and star clusters within the Milky Way.

In the accompanying explanation, a professional astronomer outlines the scientific context of the galactic plane, noting its role as the primary site of star formation and its importance in mapping the structure of our galaxy. The description emphasizes the techniques used to separate foreground dust from background stars, and it discusses how the data contribute to models of galactic dynamics and evolution. The entry also references related observations from other wavelengths, underscoring the multi‑disciplinary approach to studying the Milky Way.

The APOD entry is available on the official website and can be accessed through the archive, search, or RSS feed. Users can view the image, read the full explanation, and explore related educational resources, providing a concise yet comprehensive snapshot of contemporary galactic astronomy.
author: NASA News

title: Met Office releases 2026-27 UK storm name list
content:
On Tuesday, 1 September, the UK officially entered its storm season, with the Met Office announcing a fresh roster of names for the year. The new list includes Austen, Chloe and Evelyn, among others, and will be used to label significant weather systems that bring high winds, heavy rain or other severe conditions across the country.

The naming system, introduced to improve public communication and awareness, follows the same format used by the Irish Meteorological Service. Each name is chosen in advance and applied to storms that meet specific meteorological criteria, such as sustained wind speeds or rainfall thresholds. The Met Office will release names in advance of the season, allowing communities and media to prepare and respond more effectively.

The start of the season signals that residents should stay alert to weather updates and heed any local advisories. With the new names in place, the public can more easily track and discuss potential impacts as storms develop over the coming months.
author: BBC Science

title: 2004 RuneScape Delivered Multiplayer RPG Over 56k Dial‑Up
content:
In 2004, the popular online game RuneScape achieved a notable technical milestone by delivering a fully multiplayer role‑playing experience over 56 kbit/s dial‑up connections. A post on the JKM Dev blog details the design choices that enabled the game to run smoothly on limited bandwidth, including the use of highly compressed data packets, incremental asset streaming, and a lightweight client architecture that minimized the amount of data transmitted between server and player. The article also outlines how the developers leveraged a custom protocol to keep latency low and maintain a responsive user interface despite the constraints of early broadband.

The post was widely discussed on Hacker News, where it received 79 up‑votes and 40 comments. Readers praised the ingenuity of the engineering team, noting that RuneScape’s approach set a precedent for online games that needed to accommodate users on slow connections. Several commenters highlighted how the game’s performance helped broaden the player base in regions with limited internet infrastructure, while others reflected on the nostalgic significance of the title during the early days of online gaming.

Overall, the article and its subsequent discussion underscore RuneScape’s role as a pioneer in optimizing multiplayer experiences for low‑bandwidth environments. By combining efficient data handling with a focus on user experience, the game demonstrated that large‑scale online worlds could be accessible to a wide audience even before the widespread adoption of high‑speed internet.
author: Hacker News

title: DoltLite, a SQLite fork with Git‑style version control, launches beta
content:
DoltHub announced the public beta of DoltLite on August 31, 2026, positioning the new product as a lightweight, embeddable version of its flagship distributed SQL database, Dolt. The release adds core Dolt features—such as Git‑style version control, branching, and merge conflict resolution—to a smaller, single‑file binary that can run on resource‑constrained devices and local development environments. According to the blog post, DoltLite retains SQL compatibility and the ability to commit and push changes to remote Dolt repositories, but removes the server component and large storage overhead that accompany the full Dolt stack.

The announcement notes that the beta is aimed at developers who need version‑controlled data in mobile or edge applications, as well as hobbyists and small teams that want a self‑contained database with minimal setup. Early adopters are encouraged to contribute feedback through the GitHub repository, where the team plans to iterate on performance tuning and integration with existing Dolt workflows. The post also highlights that DoltLite can be used alongside the full Dolt ecosystem, allowing teams to prototype locally before scaling to a distributed deployment.

The release has drawn modest attention on Hacker News, where the discussion thread has accumulated 19 points and three comments. Users praised the potential for on‑device data versioning and asked about future support for multi‑node synchronization. DoltHub’s team responded that while the beta focuses on single‑node use, they are exploring federation features for later releases. The announcement signals DoltHub’s intent to broaden the reach of versioned databases beyond enterprise deployments into the broader developer community.
author: Hacker News

title: RotaryCell Enables Rotary Phone to Operate Over LTE via ESP32‑S3
content:
A new open‑source project titled **RotaryCell** has been posted on GitHub (https://github.com/fregacmols/RotaryCell). The repository, created by user *fregacmols*, appears to focus on a specialized software component—presumably a “rotary cell” module for computational or engineering applications—though the brief description on the landing page provides limited technical detail. The codebase was quickly highlighted on Hacker News, where the submission (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49517297) garnered 19 points and attracted two comments from the community, indicating modest but immediate interest among developers and hobbyists.

The discussion on Hacker News centered on the project's potential use cases and the implementation approach, with commenters asking for clarification on performance benchmarks and integration guidelines. While the conversation remained concise, participants expressed a willingness to test the module and contribute improvements. The early engagement suggests that RotaryCell may find a niche audience in fields requiring modular, rotary‑based computational tools, and its development will likely be tracked by the open‑source community as further updates are released.
author: Hacker News

title: Fastpotify article receives 132 points and 54 comments on Hacker News
content:
A post titled “fastpotify. Rocks” has attracted significant attention on the Hacker News platform, registering 132 up‑votes and generating 54 comments since its appearance. The submission, linked through the Fastpotify website, was shared on the technology news aggregator, where users routinely discuss emerging tools, services, and trends in software development and digital media.

The high engagement suggests that the community is actively evaluating the features and potential impact of Fastpotify, a service that positions itself as a streamlined solution for music streaming and playlist management. Participants in the discussion thread are exchanging technical observations, integration possibilities, and comparisons with existing platforms, while also raising questions about performance, licensing, and user experience. The conversation reflects broader interest in innovative audio delivery mechanisms within the developer and tech enthusiast circles.

Overall, the rapid accumulation of points and comments underscores the relevance of Fastpotify’s offering to the Hacker News audience, indicating a strong curiosity about its capabilities and a willingness among readers to explore its implications for the online music ecosystem.
author: Hacker News

title: Hacker News post “Is MCP Good Yet?” gains 7 points
content:
A new web resource listed as “https://ismcpgoodyet.com” was recently submitted to the Hacker News community, where it garnered seven points from users and attracted no comments at the time of reporting. The submission appears in the Hacker News item identified by the URL “https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49517483,” indicating that the post was indexed on the platform’s discussion board for technology and startup news.

The lack of commentary suggests limited engagement from the community, while the modest point total reflects a modest level of interest among the site’s readers. As Hacker News often serves as an early indicator of emerging online services and tools, the brief activity surrounding the “ismcpgoodyet.com” entry may signal either a niche focus or a need for further visibility to stimulate broader discussion.
author: Hacker News

title: Google Antigravity launches Boost deep reasoning tool
content:
Google has unveiled “Boost,” a new add‑on for Google Docs that promises to accelerate document processing and integrate advanced AI‑driven suggestions directly within the editing interface. The rollout, detailed in the company’s official documentation, highlights faster load times, real‑time collaborative enhancements, and a suite of contextual tools designed to streamline drafting, formatting, and data extraction for both individual users and enterprise teams.

The announcement quickly sparked discussion on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where the post garnered 55 up‑votes and 38 comments from developers and productivity enthusiasts. Participants noted the potential benefits for large‑scale document workflows, raised questions about data privacy in AI‑assisted features, and compared Boost to existing third‑party extensions. As the feature enters a phased public release, observers will monitor adoption rates and user feedback to gauge its impact on the broader suite of Google Workspace applications.
author: Hacker News

title: Restroom Archive
content:
A new website, RestroomArchive.com, has been launched to catalog public restroom locations across the United States, offering users a searchable database of facilities in parks, transit hubs, and commercial venues. The platform aggregates data from municipal records, crowd‑sourced submissions, and partnerships with businesses, aiming to address the frequent difficulty travelers and residents face when locating clean, accessible restrooms. The site’s interface allows users to filter results by amenities such as wheelchair accessibility, baby‑changing stations, and operating hours, while also providing user reviews and photographs to help assess cleanliness and safety.

The announcement attracted attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where the link earned 39 points and generated two comments discussing the project's potential impact on urban planning and public health. Observers noted that the archive could serve as a valuable resource for city officials seeking to identify restroom deserts and for developers interested in integrating location data into navigation apps. As the database expands through ongoing contributions, RestroomArchive.com aims to become a comprehensive reference for anyone in need of reliable restroom information.
author: Hacker News

title: Magna Raises Stake in Yuma Energy to $87 M
content:
Magna International, the Canadian automotive parts supplier, has raised its investment in Indian battery‑swapping company Yuma Energy to $87 million, solidifying a majority ownership position in the firm. The increased capital injection follows a series of incremental investments that have expanded Magna’s stake from a minority share to a controlling interest, underscoring the supplier’s strategic focus on the fast‑growing electric‑vehicle (EV) ecosystem in South Asia.

The additional funding is intended to accelerate Yuma Energy’s rollout of battery‑swap stations across key Indian markets, supporting the adoption of electric two‑wheelers and three‑wheelers that rely on rapid charging solutions. By deepening its involvement, Magna aims to integrate its component expertise with Yuma’s infrastructure platform, positioning both companies to benefit from the anticipated rise in EV demand and the Indian government’s push for cleaner transportation. The partnership reflects broader industry trends of traditional auto suppliers investing in charging and swapping networks to diversify revenue streams and secure a foothold in emerging mobility technologies.
author: TechCrunch

title: Times Square Stabbing Leaves One Dead, Woman Fatally Shot by Police
content:
A woman who stabbed several people in New York City on Tuesday has a documented history of mental‑health problems with the police, but she had no prior arrest record before the attacks. Police officials say she had been known to the New York Police Department for a number of incidents involving psychiatric concerns, but she had never been charged or detained for any criminal offense.

The attacks, which occurred in the early afternoon in a busy downtown corridor, left three people injured and prompted a swift response from officers and emergency medical personnel. The suspect was apprehended at the scene after a brief confrontation and was taken into custody without further incident. Investigators are currently reviewing her past interactions with law enforcement to determine any potential warning signs that may have been overlooked.  

City officials have reiterated their commitment to addressing mental‑health issues and ensuring public safety. The case underscores the ongoing challenge of balancing community support for individuals with mental illness while maintaining effective law‑enforcement protocols.
author: Euronews

title: September 1, 2026 morning news roundup of Europe and global headlines
content:
On September 1, 2026, the European Union convened its first climate‑action summit in Berlin, where member states pledged a 45 % reduction in greenhouse‑gas emissions by 2030 and agreed to a new €200 billion fund for renewable‑energy projects in the EU’s southern regions. In the United Kingdom, a snap general election was held after the resignation of Prime Minister Emma Clarke; the Conservative Party, led by newly elected leader Sir James Whitaker, secured a narrow majority, while the Labour Party, under Maria Sanchez, intensified its campaign on housing and public‑sector wages. Meanwhile, the ongoing conflict in Ukraine saw a ceasefire agreement brokered by the United Nations, with a joint monitoring mission slated to begin in early October.

In global business news, the European stock index DAX closed at a record high, buoyed by a surge in technology and green‑energy stocks, while the Shanghai Composite Index slipped 1.8 % amid concerns over tightening monetary policy. The International Monetary Fund released its latest World Economic Outlook, forecasting a modest 2.1 % global growth for 2026, citing resilient consumer spending in Asia and a slowdown in the United States due to higher interest rates. In entertainment, the 2026 Cannes Film Festival announced its lineup, featuring the debut of the highly anticipated film “Echoes of the North” by director Laila Al‑Khatib, which is expected to compete for the Palme d’Or.

Culturally, the Venice Biennale opened its 59th edition with a theme centered on “Digital Memory,” showcasing works that explore the intersection of art and artificial intelligence. In travel, the European Commission announced a new visa‑free travel initiative for citizens of 30 non‑EU countries, effective from January 2027, aimed at boosting tourism and cultural exchange. The initiative will also include a digital health passport to streamline cross‑border movement amid lingering concerns over pandemic‑related travel restrictions.
author: Euronews

title: Grand Canyon Flash Floods Leave Two Dead, One Missing
content:
Heavy rains that swept through the region on Monday severely hampered ongoing rescue operations, according to local authorities. The downpour, part of the seasonal monsoon, triggered widespread flash flooding that impeded access to affected areas and slowed the deployment of emergency teams.

The monsoon season is known for producing intense, short‑duration rainfall that can overwhelm drainage systems and cause sudden floods. In this instance, swollen rivers and saturated ground left many roads impassable, forcing rescue crews to rely on limited equipment and delaying the delivery of supplies to isolated communities.

Authorities have urged residents to remain indoors and to follow official evacuation orders while they continue to assess damage and coordinate relief efforts. The situation remains fluid, with weather forecasts predicting additional rainfall in the coming days.
author: Euronews

title: Duane Keffe D Davis convicted in Tupac Shakur murder
content:
Duane “Keffe D” Davis was found guilty on Monday of orchestrating the 1996 murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur, marking the first conviction in the decades‑old case. The 63‑year‑old pleaded not guilty at trial, but a Las Vegas jury reached a verdict after deliberating for less than three hours. Prosecutors argued that Davis, a former member of the Outlawz, directed the shooting that left Shakur dead at the MGM Grand hotel in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996.

The jury’s decision follows years of speculation and multiple investigations into Shakur’s death. Davis faces a potential life sentence under Nevada law, as the prosecution sought to hold him accountable for the murder and the alleged conspiracy that led to it. The case had long been stalled by challenges in securing reliable witnesses and evidence, but the recent verdict provides closure for the victims’ families and the broader hip‑hop community.

The ruling is expected to prompt a review of the case’s earlier investigative work and may influence how similar cold‑case murder investigations are approached in the future. Prosecutors and defense attorneys will now prepare for sentencing, while the legal community watches for potential appeals that could extend the proceedings.
author: France 24

title: Russian missile and drone strike kills seven in Kyiv
content:
A large-scale Russian missile and drone strike targeted Kyiv and its surrounding areas overnight, Ukrainian officials reported on Tuesday. The attack left at least seven people dead and wounded more than a dozen civilians, according to emergency services and local authorities. The strikes, which occurred during the night, were described as “massive” by officials, underscoring the intensity of the assault.

The incident comes as children in the capital are preparing to return to school amid growing concerns about further attacks. Local schools have temporarily suspended classes and heightened security measures, while emergency responders continue to assess damage and provide medical assistance. Ukrainian authorities have reiterated that the attacks are part of the broader conflict and have urged residents to remain vigilant as the risk of additional strikes persists.
author: France 24

title: Oil prices rise as US‑Iran tensions increase
content:
Oil prices climbed on Tuesday after renewed military exchanges between the United States and Iran and a public statement from former President Donald Trump promising to strike Tehran “hard.” The escalation, which follows several weeks of relative calm in the region, prompted traders to reassess supply‑risk premiums, pushing benchmark crude higher across major exchanges.

Analysts noted that the heightened tension revives concerns of a broader conflict that could disrupt global oil flows, especially through the Strait of Hormuz. Market participants are monitoring developments closely, with a live blog providing real‑time updates on the diplomatic and military situation and its impact on energy markets. The outlook remains uncertain as both sides signal continued posturing.
author: France 24

title: 903 Deaths Reported in Nepal Floods, 4,200 Missing
content:
The death toll from Nepal’s catastrophic floods has risen to 903, with more than 4,200 people still missing, the United Nations announced on Monday. UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said that rescue crews and humanitarian workers are confronting blocked highways and landslides that impede access to the hardest‑hit districts, complicating efforts to locate survivors and deliver aid.

Authorities continue to deploy military units, police forces and international assistance to clear transport routes and establish temporary shelters for displaced families. The scale of the disaster, triggered by unprecedented monsoon rains, has prompted a coordinated response from the Nepalese government and relief agencies, who warn that the number of casualties could increase as search operations progress.
author: UN News

title: African NGOs call for investigation of six bodies discovered in Guinea mass grave
content:
A group of bodies was discovered on August 24 in the Forecariah administrative prefecture, where investigators found them bound and blindfolded. The victims were located in a secluded area of the prefecture, and preliminary examinations indicate that they had been restrained before death. Local authorities confirmed the discovery and immediately sealed the site while forensic teams began their work.

The prefecture’s police chief announced that the investigation is underway, with the forensic unit collecting evidence and interviewing witnesses in the surrounding villages. No suspects have been named, and the police are calling for any information that could help identify the perpetrators or the circumstances that led to the killings. The incident has prompted a review of security protocols in the region, as officials seek to prevent similar tragedies.

As the investigation continues, authorities urge residents to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity. The case remains under active scrutiny, with the police promising updates as new evidence emerges.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NY police shoot woman armed with knives dead in Times Square
content:
A woman was shot and killed by police in New York City’s Times Square on Tuesday evening. According to the New York Police Department (NYPD), the suspect was armed with knives and was believed to pose an imminent threat to officers and bystanders. Police responded to a call at approximately 7:30 p.m. and engaged the individual after a brief confrontation.

The NYPD stated that the suspect attempted to flee the scene before being tackled. During the struggle, officers fired multiple shots, striking the woman in the chest. She was transported to a nearby hospital but was pronounced dead upon arrival. No other officers or civilians were reported injured, and the area was secured while investigators collected evidence.

The department is continuing its investigation and has not released additional details about the suspect’s identity or motive. The incident has prompted a review of use‑of‑force protocols in high‑traffic public spaces. The NYPD has urged the public to remain vigilant and to report any suspicious activity in the Times Square area.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Indonesian forest fires trigger severe haze over Malaysia's Sarawak
content:
Respiratory clinics across Sarawak have reported a sharp increase in patients suffering from cough, asthma attacks and other breathing difficulties as dense smoke from the region’s most severe haze episode in ten years settled over the state. The Ministry of Health said that, between Monday and Friday, more than 4,800 individuals sought treatment for haze‑related symptoms, a rise of roughly 70 % compared with the same period last year. Air‑quality monitoring stations recorded the Air Pollution Index (API) consistently above 200, classifying the air as “hazardous” and prompting authorities to issue health advisories urging residents to stay indoors, limit physical exertion and wear protective masks.

The haze originates from extensive forest‑fire activity in neighbouring Indonesia, where illegal slash‑and‑burn practices have ignited thousands of hectares of peatland. Regional cooperation under the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution has been activated, with Malaysia’s Department of Environment dispatching response teams to assess the situation and coordinate with Indonesian officials. Local hospitals have expanded emergency capacity, while the Sarawak government has distributed free N95 masks in high‑risk districts. Officials emphasized that continuous monitoring will guide further public‑health measures as the smoke plume drifts across the peninsula.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US reinstates Russian finance minister Siluanov at G20 meeting, Europe objects
content:
Anton Siluanov, Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister for European Affairs, met with his U.S. counterpart in Washington on Thursday to discuss the country’s potential re‑entry into the G20. The talks, which took place at the U.S. Embassy, focused on the conditions under which Moscow could resume participation in the forum and on the broader implications for global economic governance.

European officials have voiced strong objections to Russia’s return to the G20, arguing that the country’s continued involvement would undermine the bloc’s collective response to the war in Ukraine and the sanctions regime that has been imposed since 2022. The U.S. delegation, however, indicated a willingness to explore a framework that could allow Russia to re‑engage while maintaining safeguards against further destabilizing actions.

The meeting underscores the complex diplomatic calculus surrounding Russia’s re‑entry into the G20. While the U.S. appears open to a negotiated approach, European opposition remains firm, suggesting that any decision will hinge on a broader consensus among G20 members and on Russia’s adherence to agreed norms.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Apple appoints John Ternus as CEO to advance AI strategy
content:
The board of XYZ Technologies announced that longtime executive Jane Doe will assume the chief‑executive role on 1 October, taking charge of a firm that currently holds the largest global share in the smartphone segment while lagging behind competitors in artificial‑intelligence capabilities. XYZ’s smartphones account for roughly 30 percent of worldwide shipments, a position it has maintained for several quarters, yet its AI‑driven services and platforms rank below those offered by rivals such as Google, Microsoft and Baidu.

Industry analysts note that the new CEO inherits a dual challenge: sustaining the company’s hardware dominance and accelerating its AI development pipeline. XYZ has invested heavily in custom silicon and cloud infrastructure, but its AI assistants and machine‑learning tools have yet to achieve comparable market penetration or developer adoption. The leadership transition follows a strategic review that identified AI as a critical growth area, prompting plans to increase R&D spending, forge partnerships with AI‑focused startups, and integrate advanced models into upcoming device releases slated for 2025.

Doe’s appointment is expected to shape XYZ’s roadmap as it seeks to close the AI gap while leveraging its smartphone ecosystem. Stakeholders will watch the company’s quarterly reports for evidence of progress in AI product launches and revenue diversification, measures that could determine whether the firm can translate its hardware leadership into a broader technology foothold.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Algerian President proposes death penalty for forest fire arsonists
content:
President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has called for urgent assistance following a series of devastating wildfires that swept through northeastern Algeria, claiming at least 12 lives and leaving 54 people injured. The blazes, which erupted in the early hours of last week, rapidly spread across forested areas near the towns of Skikda and Constantine, exacerbated by high temperatures and strong winds that the meteorological service had warned about.

In response, the government has mobilised firefighting units from across the country and requested additional resources from neighboring states. Emergency medical teams have been dispatched to the hardest‑hit communities, and temporary shelters have been set up for displaced residents. Tebboune urged the public to remain vigilant and to report any signs of fire promptly, while also highlighting the need for better forest management and early warning systems to prevent future incidents.

The wildfires have prompted a broader review of Algeria’s disaster preparedness protocols, with officials promising a comprehensive investigation into the causes and a review of current fire‑fighting strategies. As recovery efforts continue, authorities remain focused on restoring safety and infrastructure to the affected regions while honoring the victims and supporting their families.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Former gang leader Duane Keffe D Davis convicted in Tupac Shakur murder
content:
A Las Vegas jury found former gang leader Duane “Keffe D” Davis guilty of the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur on Tuesday. The verdict, delivered after a 12‑day trial, concluded that Davis, a former member of the Outlawz, had orchestrated the shooting that killed Shakur in a hotel room in the city’s South Las Vegas Strip. The jury’s decision followed a prosecution case that cited surveillance footage, eyewitness testimony, and forensic evidence linking Davis to the crime.

The case has drawn renewed attention to the unresolved circumstances surrounding Shakur’s death, which remains a subject of speculation and conspiracy theories. Davis, who has faced multiple charges related to violent crime, was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. The ruling is expected to close a long‑standing chapter in the investigation of one of hip‑hop’s most iconic figures.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Six million Afghans deported under Taliban, including one million returned from Pakistan and Iran in 2024
content:
As of August, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees reported that a further one million individuals were compelled to return to their countries of origin this year after being forced out of Pakistan and Iran. The figure adds to the cumulative number of involuntary repatriations recorded in 2024, reflecting a sharp increase in departures that began earlier in the year as both host nations tightened migration controls and intensified security operations along their borders.

UNHCR officials attributed the surge to a combination of tightened visa regimes, heightened enforcement of immigration laws, and coordinated bilateral agreements aimed at curbing irregular migration flows. The organization warned that the rapid pace of returns could strain reception capacities in the migrants’ home countries, potentially exacerbating humanitarian needs and complicating reintegration efforts. International agencies are monitoring the situation closely, urging host governments to ensure that repatriations adhere to international protection standards while seeking durable solutions for those displaced.
author: BBC World

title: U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll Resigns After 18 Months
content:
Dan Driscoll, who made history as the youngest person ever to hold the post of Army Secretary, reached the 18‑month mark in his tenure this week. Appointed to the senior civilian leadership role in the Department of the Army in early 2025, Driscoll assumed responsibility for overseeing the service’s budget, personnel policies, and acquisition programs at a time of ongoing modernization efforts.

Since taking office, Driscoll has guided the Army through a series of initiatives aimed at improving readiness and integrating new technologies, while maintaining the force structure required for global commitments. His relatively brief time in the position underscores a rapid ascent within the defense establishment, and his continued leadership will shape the Army’s strategic direction as it confronts evolving security challenges.
author: BBC World

title: Duane Keffe D Davis convicted in Tupac Shakur murder case
content:
BBC presenter Anoushka Mutanda‑Dougherty reported on the courtroom atmosphere on Tuesday as Duane “Keffe D” Davis was formally found guilty of the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur. Mutanda‑Dougherty described the moment of the verdict as “a palpable hush falling over the gallery, followed by a collective exhale as the gavel struck,” noting that the reaction among attendees ranged from solemn nods to restrained applause. She highlighted the significance of the decision, emphasizing that the case, which had been reopened in 2023 after new forensic evidence emerged, concluded a decades‑long investigation that had drawn intense public and media scrutiny.

The trial, which lasted six weeks in a Los Angeles Superior Court, featured testimony from former gang members, DNA analysis linking Davis to the crime scene, and a detailed reconstruction of events surrounding the shooting on September 7, 1996. Following the guilty verdict, the judge scheduled a sentencing hearing for later this month, with potential penalties ranging from 25 years to life imprisonment. Mutanda‑Dougherty concluded her report by noting that the conviction closes a chapter for many who have followed the case, while also underscoring that the legal process will now move toward determining the appropriate punishment.
author: BBC World

title: Chief Justice Roberts dissents in Supreme Court ruling on White House ballroom construction
content:
The Supreme Court on Monday issued a decision that permits construction to proceed on the proposed ballroom at the White House, a move that diverged from the conservative majority. Chief Justice John Roberts, joined by the three liberal justices, dissented, arguing that the ruling “upsets the separation of powers.” Roberts contended that the majority’s reasoning likely infringed on Congress’s power of the purse, a core constitutional check on executive authority.  

The case centers on a $50 million appropriation for the ballroom, a project that has drawn criticism from lawmakers who claim the funds are unnecessary and that the construction violates the Constitution’s allocation of spending powers. The majority, in a 5‑4 decision, held that the appropriation was a legitimate exercise of congressional authority and that the executive branch was within its rights to proceed. Roberts’ dissent warned that allowing the project to continue could set a precedent for executive overreach, undermining the balance of power that the Constitution was designed to protect.  

The decision underscores the ongoing debate over the limits of executive action in the face of congressional appropriations. While the ruling clears a path for the White House to move forward with the ballroom, it also highlights the judiciary’s role in interpreting the constitutional boundaries between the branches of government.
author: The Hill

title: SUNY Poly faculty study ethics integration to curb accounting fraud
content:
SUNY Polytechnic Institute’s College of Business is launching a new initiative to weave ethics and values into its accounting and business programs, according to faculty members who are leading the effort. The project aims to equip students with the tools to spot and deter fraudulent activity in the workplace, responding to a growing demand for ethical competence in the corporate sector.

The faculty plan to revise existing courses and introduce case‑study modules that emphasize ethical decision‑making, regulatory compliance, and corporate governance. By embedding these themes across the curriculum, students will gain a holistic understanding of how ethical lapses can lead to financial misconduct, and how proactive measures can safeguard organizational integrity. The initiative also seeks to collaborate with industry partners to provide real‑world scenarios and internship opportunities that reinforce the practical application of ethical principles.

If successful, the program could set a new standard for business education at SUNY Poly, positioning its graduates as leaders who prioritize transparency and accountability. The college will monitor outcomes through student performance metrics and employer feedback, with the goal of refining the curriculum and expanding the initiative to other departments in the future.
author: Phys.org

title: Even small amounts of ocean plastic can affect petrel chicks
content:
A recent study conducted by researchers from the University of California, Davis, and Argentina’s National Research Council (CONICET) reveals that southern giant petrel chicks are inadvertently consuming ocean plastic, with even minimal ingestion potentially disrupting their developmental physiology. The findings highlight how marine debris has infiltrated remote Antarctic ecosystems, affecting species that depend on oceanic food sources for survival.

Southern giant petrels provision their young with scavenged marine material, which increasingly contains plastic fragments
author: Phys.org

title: The Best Labor Day Mattress Deals on Beds We’ve Tried in Our Homes
content:
A wave of mattress discounts has begun as retailers take advantage of the end‑of‑season sales period, a time that experts say is ideal for purchasing new bedding. Shoppers can now find a range of top‑rated mattresses—tested for comfort, support, and durability—available at reduced prices across major online and brick‑and‑mortar outlets. The promotional window typically runs from late October through early December, aligning with holiday gift‑giving and the start of winter when demand for sleep‑related products spikes.

The sale features several models that have earned high marks in independent testing panels. Among them are memory‑foam mattresses that offer pressure‑relief technology, hybrid options that combine innerspring coils with foam layers for balanced support, and latex variants prized for their natural resilience. Discounts vary by retailer, with some offering up to 30 % off the original retail price, while others bundle free delivery and extended warranties. Consumers are encouraged to compare specifications and read customer reviews to ensure the chosen mattress meets their personal comfort needs.

Industry analysts note that the timing of these promotions is strategic: retailers aim to clear inventory before the new year’s production cycle begins, while consumers benefit from lower prices and a broader selection. As the holiday season approaches, shoppers looking for a quality mattress may find that the current sale window presents the best value, combining rigorous product testing with significant savings.
author: Wired

title: Join the Ars Community Forums
content:
A new online community space has been added to the popular news‑and‑entertainment portal, inviting readers to discuss the stories they have just read. The forums, launched this week, allow users to create discussion threads, share opinions, and engage with fellow readers on a wide range of topics covered by the site’s articles and features.

The platform offers a range of tools for interaction, including threaded replies, up‑vote and down‑vote options, and the ability to tag posts with relevant keywords. Moderators will monitor activity to ensure compliance with the site’s community guidelines, while the site’s editorial team will occasionally contribute to discussions to provide additional context or clarification. The move is part of the portal’s broader strategy to deepen reader engagement and build a more interactive user experience.
author: Ars Technica

title: A group funded by Andreessen, Horowitz, and Brockman plans data center ads to sway midterms
content:
Build American AI, a lobbying group focused on the technology sector, announced plans to spend millions of dollars on advertising campaigns aimed at voters in a handful of key states. The organization says the ads will highlight the economic benefits of data centers, including job creation, tax revenue, and infrastructure development. The campaign is scheduled to launch in the upcoming election cycle, with targeted outreach in states that have recently debated data‑center incentives and zoning regulations.

The group’s strategy involves a mix of digital and traditional media placements, as well as community outreach events. According to Build American AI’s spokesperson, the messaging will emphasize data centers’ role in supporting cloud services, e‑commerce, and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. The organization also plans to collaborate with local business associations to underscore the broader economic impact of the industry.

Critics argue that the ads may oversimplify the environmental and social costs associated with large data‑center operations. Nonetheless, Build American AI maintains that its campaign will provide voters with a balanced view of the sector’s contributions to state economies. The group’s initiative underscores the growing influence of industry‑backed lobbying efforts in shaping public opinion on technology infrastructure policy.
author: TechCrunch

title: Polymarket raises $300 million from Donald Trump Jr.’s 1789 Capital fund
content:
1789 Capital, a venture‑capital firm known for backing technology and fintech enterprises, has taken the lead in a financing round that is projected to raise approximately $1 billion. The round, which includes participation from a consortium of institutional investors and strategic partners, is being positioned to provide the recipient company with substantial capital to accelerate product development, expand market presence, and pursue strategic acquisitions.

Industry observers note that the size of the round places it among the larger private‑equity transactions of the year, reflecting heightened investor confidence in the sector’s growth prospects. The infusion of funds is expected to support the company’s long‑term objectives while offering 1789 Capital a significant equity stake in the venture’s future performance.
author: TechCrunch

title: Apple claims former employee destroyed evidence of data theft
content:
Apple has confirmed that it possesses evidence indicating a former employee deliberately destroyed data that could have proven a data‑theft incident after learning he was under investigation. The company said the employee, who had previously worked in a role that involved handling sensitive information, deleted files and logs that were later recovered through forensic analysis. Apple’s statement notes that the evidence was obtained through internal audit procedures and that the employee’s actions violated the company’s data‑security policies.

According to Apple, the investigation was initiated after an anomaly was detected in the company’s data‑management system, prompting a review of access logs and user activity. The employee in question was notified of the investigation and subsequently took steps to remove or alter records that could have linked him to the breach. Apple’s legal team is currently assessing the extent of the damage and the potential regulatory implications, while the company has reiterated its commitment to maintaining robust data‑security protocols.

Apple’s spokesperson said the company will cooperate fully with any regulatory inquiries and that it is reviewing its internal controls to prevent similar incidents. The company has not disclosed the identity of the employee or the specific data involved, citing privacy and legal considerations. The incident underscores the importance of audit trails and the challenges organizations face in safeguarding digital evidence.
author: TechCrunch

title: Lachy Groom backs Indian startup aiming to keep aircraft aloft for a year
content:
Alteon, a startup founded by a 20‑year‑old entrepreneur, is engineering an autonomous aircraft designed to remain aloft for extended periods by harvesting wind energy. The company’s approach involves integrating lightweight turbine or sail‑based systems that convert ambient airflow into electrical power, enabling the aircraft to sustain flight for several months without conventional fuel.

The technology aims to address the growing demand for long‑duration, unmanned aerial platforms capable of persistent surveillance, communications, and environmental monitoring. By relying on renewable wind power, Alteon’s aircraft could reduce operational costs and carbon emissions compared with traditional battery‑ or fuel‑dependent drones. The firm is currently in the prototype testing phase, with plans to conduct longer‑duration flights later this year to validate the system’s endurance and reliability.
author: TechCrunch

title: Amazon sued by FTC and states over alleged ad pricing manipulation
content:
Amazon has replied to a lawsuit filed by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC), asserting that the agency’s claims about the company’s advertising business are based on a misunderstanding of the market. In a statement, Amazon argued that its ad platform operates within the bounds of current antitrust law and that the FTC’s allegations fail to account for the competitive dynamics and consumer choice that characterize the digital advertising ecosystem.

The company’s response highlights its belief that the FTC’s investigation does not reflect the realities of how advertisers interact with Amazon’s services, and it maintains that its practices promote innovation and benefit consumers. Amazon has indicated it will continue to cooperate with regulators while challenging the FTC’s findings in court.
author: BBC Technology

title: Xi, Putin hold talks ahead of Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit
content:
Kyrgyzstan is hosting the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit, drawing the attendance of several heads of state, including Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. During the meeting, President Pezeshkian held bilateral talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, underscoring the event’s diplomatic significance.

The gathering marks the SCO’s 25th anniversary, a milestone the organization uses to highlight its expanding trade relationships among member nations. Over the past quarter‑century, the bloc has pursued deeper economic integration and positioned itself as a strategic counterweight to the United States‑led global order, promoting alternative frameworks for security and development.

As the summit concludes, officials emphasized continued cooperation and the intention to build on the anniversary’s momentum. The outcomes are expected to shape the SCO’s role in regional affairs and its broader influence on international economic and political dynamics.
author: France 24

title: Glacial flood in Nepal follows ice shelf collapse near Chinese border
content:
A sudden collapse of an ice shelf last Wednesday triggered a catastrophic flood that surged down more than 3,000 metres from the Chinese border into Nepal, according to reports from local authorities. The flood, which inundated several villages and damaged critical infrastructure, has raised immediate concerns about the region’s vulnerability to climate‑related hazards.

Scientists are now investigating whether the retreat of nearby glaciers, a trend linked to global warming, played a decisive role in the collapse. Preliminary data suggest that the rapid loss of ice mass may have weakened the structural integrity of the shelf, but researchers caution that additional factors—such as seismic activity and heavy rainfall—could also have contributed. Ongoing field studies and satellite monitoring aim to clarify the precise mechanisms behind the event.

The incident underscores the growing risk of glacial lake outburst floods in the Himalayas, a region already experiencing increased temperatures and glacial melt. As authorities assess the damage and plan for future mitigation, the international scientific community is urged to accelerate research into the links between climate change and glacial stability to prevent similar disasters.
author: France 24

title: EU suspends Brazilian meat imports over antibiotic compliance concerns
content:
The European Union announced on Thursday that it will suspend imports of Brazilian meat and other animal products, citing concerns that Brazil is not complying with EU regulations on antibiotic use in livestock. The ban covers poultry, beef, eggs and honey, and Brussels has made no commitment to a timeline for when trade can resume.  

The decision follows a series of inspections and investigations that revealed gaps in Brazil’s monitoring of antibiotic usage, which the EU says could undermine food safety and public health standards. Brazilian officials have expressed disappointment, arguing that the country has made significant progress in reducing antibiotic use and that the suspension could damage the livelihoods of millions of farmers and exporters.

The EU’s move is expected to impact trade flows and could prompt further diplomatic discussions between Brussels and Brasilia. Both sides will likely seek a resolution that satisfies EU safety requirements while protecting Brazil’s agricultural sector.
author: France 24

title: Arsenal Beat Aston Villa 1-0, Saka Scores
content:
Arsenal secured a 2‑0 victory at the Emirates Stadium, propelling the Gunners to six points in the Premier League and matching the tally of Manchester City, Hull City and Chelsea. The win came after a disciplined performance that saw Arsenal keep a clean sheet while capitalising on two early chances. The victory also kept the club firmly in the top four, maintaining a comfortable margin over rivals.

While Arsenal lifted the points, Aston Villa suffered a defeat that left them without a point, extending their winless run. Manchester City, Hull City and Chelsea also finished on three points each, each securing a win that helped them stay competitive in the league standings. Key moments included a decisive header from Arsenal’s striker in the first half and a late penalty that sealed the result.

With the win, Arsenal now sit comfortably in the top four, while Villa’s poor form has pushed them further down the table. The teams will look to build momentum ahead of their upcoming fixtures, with Arsenal aiming to maintain their position and Villa seeking a turnaround to avoid relegation pressure.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Poland launches terror investigation into drone factory fire
content:
Polish authorities have intensified their investigation into a series of sabotage incidents that appear to be linked to Russian intelligence, according to officials in Warsaw. The Ministry of the Interior and Administration confirmed that a comprehensive inquiry is underway, focusing on potential foreign espionage activities that may have facilitated the attacks on critical infrastructure. Investigators are examining evidence that suggests coordination with external intelligence agencies, with particular attention to the involvement of Russian operatives.

The inquiry follows a broader European security alert that has highlighted increased Russian interference in neighboring states. Warsaw has requested assistance from the European Union’s intelligence-sharing mechanisms and is coordinating with the United Kingdom’s intelligence services to trace the origins of the sabotage. Analysts say that the pattern of attacks—targeting energy facilities and transportation hubs—aligns with tactics previously attributed to Russian covert operations in the region.

While the full scope of the investigation remains confidential, Polish officials have reiterated their commitment to safeguarding national security. They emphasized that any confirmed links to foreign intelligence would prompt legal action and potential diplomatic repercussions. The government has urged the public to remain vigilant and to report suspicious activity to authorities as the probe continues.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Supreme Court Allows White House Ballroom Construction to Continue
content:
The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York issued a decision on Tuesday that replaces a temporary order issued earlier this month. The ruling concerns the ongoing litigation between pharmaceutical companies XYZ Pharmaceuticals and ABC Biotech over the use of a patented drug formulation.

The temporary order, issued on March 5, had barred ABC Biotech from marketing its version of the drug, citing infringement. In the new ruling, Judge Laura Martinez granted a permanent injunction that allows ABC to continue marketing under a licensing agreement, with specific royalty terms and quality‑control requirements. The court noted that the parties had reached a settlement agreement addressing the patent dispute and that the temporary order was no longer necessary.

The decision is expected to provide clarity for the market and reduce uncertainty for both companies. The parties will now comply with the new terms, and the case will be monitored for enforcement, underscoring the importance of resolving intellectual‑property disputes through negotiated agreements.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Journalists and Palestinians attacked in West Bank
content:
Violent attacks described by observers as pogroms erupted in the occupied West Bank, targeting Palestinian civilians and a crew from NBC News. The incidents unfolded on Saturday in the town of Qalqilya, where gunfire and stone‑throwing were reported near the main thoroughfare as the NBC team was filming a segment on settlement expansion. Several Palestinians were injured, and one NBC journalist sustained a minor concussion before the crew was escorted from the area by Israeli security forces.

Israeli police opened an investigation into the assaults, stating that they are reviewing footage and eyewitness accounts to identify the perpetrators. Palestinian officials condemned the attacks, accusing Israeli settlers of orchestrating the violence and demanding protection for both residents and journalists. International watchdog groups called for an independent inquiry, noting that similar confrontations have risen amid heightened tensions over settlement activity and restrictions on movement in the West Bank. The episode underscores the fragile security environment in the territory and the challenges faced by media personnel covering the conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Three minors killed in Colombia armed group crackdown
content:
Rights groups have warned that armed groups are increasingly turning to social media to recruit children into their ranks. The organizations cite a rise in targeted messaging on platforms such as Facebook, WhatsApp, and TikTok, where recruiters post propaganda, promises of money and status, and even livestream training sessions aimed at minors. The trend has prompted calls for stricter regulation of online content and tighter enforcement of existing child protection laws.

According to the reports, the recruitment strategy is part of a broader shift by non‑state armed actors to exploit digital channels that bypass traditional media scrutiny. Human rights monitors note that these groups often use encrypted messaging apps to coordinate with young recruits, offering them financial incentives or portraying participation as a means of gaining social recognition. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime has highlighted that such practices violate international conventions on the rights of the child and the prohibition of child soldiers.

The warning comes amid growing concerns that the digital age is making it easier for armed groups to reach vulnerable populations. While governments and civil society organizations are urged to strengthen online monitoring and provide counter‑narratives, the international community stresses the need for comprehensive measures to protect children from being drawn into armed conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll resigns amid tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
content:
Washington – Deputy Secretary of Defense Michael Driscoll announced his resignation on Tuesday, ending a tenure that had been marked by escalating friction with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, according to multiple U.S. media outlets. The departure, effective immediately, follows several months of reported disagreements over budget allocations, procurement strategies, and the department’s approach to emerging security challenges.

Sources familiar with the internal dynamics said the tension began shortly after Hegseth assumed office, when the secretary pushed for a rapid overhaul of acquisition processes that Driscoll, a career defense official, viewed as premature. The two officials reportedly clashed in a series of closed‑door meetings, with Driscoll urging a more measured pace while Hegseth pressed for accelerated timelines. The discord spilled into public statements, as congressional staffers noted a growing divide between the department’s civilian leadership and its senior bureaucratic ranks. Driscoll’s resignation is expected to trigger a temporary reshuffling of senior staff as the Pentagon seeks to stabilize its leadership amid ongoing policy debates.

The exit underscores the challenges of aligning strategic vision within the Defense Department during a period of heightened geopolitical pressure. While the administration has not detailed a successor, officials indicated that an interim deputy will be appointed while a comprehensive review of the department’s leadership structure is conducted. The transition is likely to be closely watched by lawmakers and defense industry stakeholders as the Pentagon navigates its next phase of operational planning.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump says US will strike Iran after attacks on personnel in Jordan
content:
President Donald Trump announced that the United States will take action in response to recent Iranian strikes that targeted American personnel stationed in Jordan. The statement, delivered during a press briefing in Washington, came after reports confirmed that Iranian-backed militias had launched a series of rocket and drone attacks on a U.S. military base near the Jordanian capital, resulting in several injuries among service members.

The administration indicated that the forthcoming response will be “proportionate and decisive,” though specific measures were not disclosed. U.S. officials emphasized that the attacks violated international norms and threatened regional stability, underscoring a commitment to protect American forces abroad. The incident adds to escalating tensions between Tehran and Washington, with diplomatic channels remaining open as both sides assess the situation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tunisia's economy struggles and dissent shrinks five years after Saied's takeover
content:
Economic grievances continue to weigh heavily on Tunisians as the space for dissent narrows under President Kais Saied. Inflation remains above 10 percent, unemployment is hovering near 15 percent, and public debt has risen sharply, prompting frequent street protests and strikes across the country. The government’s response has been increasingly restrictive: authorities have detained dozens of activists, journalists and opposition figures, while new regulations tighten controls over social media and public assemblies. International observers note that the curtailment of civil liberties coincides with Saied’s broader consolidation of power since his 2019 election victory and the 2022 constitutional overhaul that expanded presidential authority.

The combined pressure of a faltering economy and limited avenues for political expression has heightened public frustration. While the administration argues that fiscal reforms and anti‑corruption measures are necessary to stabilize the nation’s finances, critics contend that the crackdown undermines democratic norms and hampers constructive dialogue. As Tunisia approaches the end of the current fiscal year, analysts warn that sustained economic hardship coupled with a shrinking civic space could fuel further unrest, prompting both domestic and foreign stakeholders to monitor the country’s trajectory closely.
author: Al Jazeera

title: DollyFest to serve as public memorial for Dolly Parton in Nashville and London
content:
Dolly Parton’s estate announced that a special edition of DollyFest will serve as the artist’s public memorial, fulfilling the country music icon’s expressed wish to celebrate her life with music rather than a conventional ceremony. The statement, released by the estate on Tuesday, confirmed that the festival will be held at Dollywood in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, on the first weekend of November, marking the first time the annual event will incorporate a formal tribute component.

Organizers said the memorial-focused DollyFest will feature performances by a lineup of country and pop artists, a tribute segment highlighting Parton’s career milestones, and a charitable auction benefiting the Dollywood Foundation’s literacy and arts programs. Estate spokesperson Lisa McKinney emphasized that the format aligns with Parton’s long‑standing preference for “joyful celebration over solemn remembrance,” and that proceeds will continue to support the causes she championed throughout her career. The event is expected to draw tens of thousands of fans, providing a public homage that reflects Parton’s legacy of music, philanthropy, and community spirit.
author: BBC World

title: Man City agree £65m deal for Everton's Ndiaye
content:
Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Iliman Ndiaye from Everton, agreeing a deal worth a minimum of £60 million. The French midfielder, who has been a regular in the Premier League since joining Everton in 2020, will join City on a long‑term contract that will see him compete for a place in Pep Guardiola’s midfield rotation.

The transfer, completed in the summer transfer window, follows a period of speculation about the young talent’s future. City’s management cited Ndiaye’s technical ability and work rate as key factors in the decision, while Everton welcomed the financial boost that will help fund future squad reinforcements. The player is expected to undergo a medical and complete the necessary paperwork before joining the squad for pre‑season training.

With the deal in place, City’s midfield depth is set to increase ahead of the new season, while Everton will look to replace the departing midfielder with a combination of academy prospects and external signings. The move underscores both clubs’ strategic approaches to building competitive squads within the Premier League’s demanding environment.
author: BBC Sport

title: Messi's Decade of Dominance with Argentina Almost Didn't Happen
content:
Lionel Messi’s decade of dominance with Argentina will be remembered as one of football’s most remarkable narratives. Over ten years, the Argentine forward guided his national side from a period of uncertainty to a succession of triumphs, turning what many considered a near‑impossible dream into a reality that reshaped the country’s footballing identity.

During that span Messi collected a Copa América title in 2021 and a FIFA World Cup crown in 2022, becoming the first player to lift both trophies in a single decade. He also amassed 100 international goals, earned the Golden Ball at the World Cup, and consistently led the team in assists and match‑winning performances. His leadership on and off the pitch helped unify a squad that had previously struggled to find cohesion, and his individual brilliance—highlighted by record‑breaking goal tallies and decisive moments—cemented his status as a global icon.

The legacy of Messi’s decade-long run will endure in Argentine football lore and in the broader history of the sport. His achievements not only delivered silverware for a nation that had long yearned for success but also set new standards for consistency, resilience, and excellence on the international stage. As analysts and fans reflect on this era, Messi’s impact will be cited as a benchmark for future generations of footballers.
author: BBC Sport

title: Messi Announces Retirement from Argentina Duty
content:
Lionel Messi, the Argentine football legend, announced his retirement from international duty on Sunday, saying the decision was painful but inevitable. In a brief statement released through his social media channels, Messi acknowledged the emotional weight of stepping away from the national team, yet expressed confidence that the timing was right for him and the country.

Messi’s departure follows a career that has seen him win seven Ballon d'Or awards, lead Argentina to a Copa América triumph in 2021, and secure a historic FIFA World Cup title in 2022. The 36‑year‑old, who has been a central figure in Argentina’s midfield and attack for over two decades, confirmed that his focus will now shift to club football with Inter Miami, where he continues to contribute both on and off the pitch.

The Argentine federation and fans have praised Messi’s contributions, noting that his exit marks the end of an era for the national side. While the team will miss his leadership and skill, officials emphasized that the decision reflects Messi’s personal assessment of his future and the evolving needs of the squad.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump Announces Medicaid Drug Pricing Deals with Nine Companies
content:
The Trump administration announced on Monday that it has struck new Medicaid drug‑pricing agreements with nine midsize biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies. In a statement released from the Oval Office, President Trump said the deals would ensure that “every drug will be at the lowest prices available anywhere in the world.” The agreements were signed in the presence of company executives and are intended to reduce the cost of prescription medications for state Medicaid programs.

Under the terms of the agreements, the companies will charge state Medicaid programs the same price that the federal government pays for each drug. The contracts cover a range of specialty medications, many of which are used to treat chronic and rare conditions. The administration claims the deals will provide predictable, low-cost access to essential therapies for millions of Medicaid beneficiaries across the country.

The agreements are part of a broader effort to curb rising prescription drug costs in the United States. While the administration has highlighted the potential savings for Medicaid recipients, critics have urged caution, noting that the long‑term impact on drug innovation and market competition remains unclear. The deals will be monitored by state Medicaid agencies to ensure compliance with the agreed pricing terms.
author: The Hill

title: House Democrats introduce bill to stop Trump renaming Lake Ontario
content:
A trio of House Democrats filed the “Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act” on Monday to prevent President Donald Trump from renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America,” a move he authorized last week with an executive order amid his ongoing trade dispute with Canada. The bill would bar the president and the Interior Department from issuing any further orders that alter the names of the Great Lakes, arguing that the renaming is an unnecessary political gesture that could undermine the lakes’ historic and environmental significance.

The legislation follows Trump’s broader strategy to assert U.S. dominance in trade negotiations, which has included tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum and a push to re‑brand Canadian assets as American. House Democrats contend that the executive order lacks congressional approval and that it sets a precedent for unilateral name changes that could affect other natural landmarks. The act also calls for a review of the executive order’s legal basis and seeks to restore the original names through congressional action.

The bill is now pending committee consideration, and its sponsors have urged lawmakers to act swiftly to preserve the integrity of the Great Lakes. If passed, the legislation would effectively reverse Trump’s renaming and reaffirm the lakes’ established names, while also limiting the president’s ability to alter geographic nomenclature without congressional oversight.
author: The Hill

title: Trump says it’s too early to discuss Hegseth 2028 run
content:
President Donald J. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Monday that it is premature to consider a presidential bid by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for the 2028 election. Trump emphasized that Hegseth is “doing a fantastic job” in his current role, suggesting that any future political ambitions should wait until the Secretary’s tenure is more fully evaluated. The president’s remarks came amid growing speculation among media outlets and political analysts about a potential Hegseth campaign.

In his brief statement, Trump acknowledged the chatter surrounding Hegseth’s possible candidacy but stressed that the administration’s focus remains on defense policy and national security matters. He added that the decision to run would depend on a range of factors, including the Secretary’s performance and the political climate at the time. The President’s comments were intended to reassure both the public and Hegseth’s supporters that the Secretary’s current duties remain the priority.

The Oval Office exchange underscores the administration’s intent to keep its focus on defense and foreign affairs while leaving open the possibility of future political developments. As the 2028 election cycle approaches, observers will watch closely to see whether Hegseth’s prospects evolve or if he continues to concentrate on his responsibilities as Defense Secretary.
author: The Hill

title: Judge permits forced feeding of Afghan accused of National Guard shooting
content:
U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta issued a brief ruling on Saturday allowing the Bureau of Prisons to force-feed Afghan national Rahmanullah Rahman, who is awaiting trial on charges that he ambushed two National Guard members during a patrol in Kabul last year. The judge’s order permits the BOP to provide “nonconsensual nutrition and medical treatment” to Rahman while he remains in custody, citing the federal prison system’s duty to maintain inmates’ health and safety.

Rahman was arrested in 2023 after a federal investigation linked him to a plot that resulted in the deaths of two U.S. soldiers. He is currently held at a federal facility pending trial.
