The system’s reliance on large, centralized processing facilities, extensive interstate distribution networks, and a growing share of imported produce creates multiple points where pathogens such as Salmonella, E. coli, Cyclospora and Giardia can enter and spread. Additional factors—including labor shortages in inspection crews, limited real‑time traceability technology, and seasonal temperature spikes that favor bacterial growth—compound the vulnerability, making rapid detection and response more challenging.

Officials emphasize that addressing the current outbreak will require both restored funding for inspection and regulatory programs and longer‑term reforms to improve supply‑chain transparency, bolster sanitation standards, and enhance monitoring of high‑risk foods. Without such measures, the United States remains exposed to recurring episodes of foodborne disease.
author: Wired

title: Former Rep. George Santos receives lifetime ban from Kalshi and $71,000 fine
content:
A former U.S. Representative has been fined more than $71,000 after an investigation found that the individual had attempted to manipulate a prediction market. The fine was imposed by the relevant U.S. regulatory authority following a review of the Representative’s trading activity and communications that suggested an effort to influence market outcomes for personal gain.

The investigation revealed that the former lawmaker used insider information and coordinated trades to shift the odds on a popular prediction platform that tracks political events. The regulatory body cited violations of market‑fairness rules and concluded that the actions undermined the integrity of the market. The fine represents the maximum penalty under the applicable statutes for such conduct, and the Representative has been barred from participating in any regulated trading activity for a period of time.

The enforcement action underscores the broader effort to maintain transparency and fairness in prediction markets. It serves as a reminder that former public officials are subject to the same regulatory standards as other market participants, and it signals that attempts to manipulate market outcomes will be met with significant penalties.
author: Wired

title: Asus ProArt 27 QD‑OLED (PA279cdv) Review: Affordable HDR Display
content:
Asus has unveiled a new monitor aimed at video‑editing professionals that supports full high‑dynamic‑range (HDR) playback, offering an alternative to the higher‑cost OLED panels that have traditionally dominated the market. The display features a 4K resolution panel with HDR10 certification, a peak brightness of 600 nits, and a wide color gamut covering 99 percent of the DCI‑P3 spectrum, enabling creators to work with accurate, vibrant images without the premium price tag associated with OLED technology. Priced in the mid‑range segment, the monitor positions itself as a more accessible option for freelancers, small studios, and other users who require HDR‑capable editing tools but have been constrained by budget.

Industry analysts note that the introduction of an HDR‑ready, non‑OLED monitor expands the toolkit available to content creators, potentially lowering the barrier to high‑quality video production. By combining a high refresh rate, low input lag, and factory‑calibrated color accuracy, the Asus model seeks to meet the demands of professional workflows while remaining within reach of a broader audience. The launch reflects a growing trend toward more affordable, high‑performance displays that cater to the evolving needs of the digital media industry.
author: Wired

title: New York governor vows action against Cody Wilson's 3D‑printed gun circumvention tool
content:
Cody Wilson, the inventor of the first 3‑D printed handgun, unveiled a new software tool last week that is designed to bypass a New York law banning the production of firearms with 3‑D printers. The announcement, which included a taunt directed at Governor Kathy Hochul, sparked immediate backlash from state officials. Hochul responded in an episode of the podcast *Decoder*, stating that she would not allow the tool to undermine New York’s gun‑control legislation. She emphasized that the law explicitly prohibits the creation of 3‑D printed guns within the state and that she would take steps to enforce it.

The governor’s remarks came as part of a broader effort to tighten enforcement of the 2023 New York law, which was enacted in response to the proliferation of homemade firearms. Hochul noted that she could not always be at the forefront of every attempt to circumvent the law, but she assured residents that the state would pursue legal and regulatory measures to prevent the use of the new tool. She also warned Wilson that the state would “get ahead of him” and that any attempt to facilitate illegal gun manufacturing would be met with swift action.

The incident highlights the ongoing tension between technology developers and lawmakers over the regulation of 3‑D printed weapons. While Wilson’s tool represents a new frontier in illicit firearms production, the state’s response underscores a commitment to enforcing existing gun‑control statutes. As the debate continues, New York remains poised to take further steps to close loopholes and protect public safety.
author: The Verge

title: Sony WH‑1000XM5 headphones now $198 in Labor Day sale
content:
Labor Day is a prime time for tech bargains, and Sony’s week‑long sale on its last‑generation WH‑1000XM5 headphones stands out as one of the most compelling offers. The over‑ear headphones, known for their premium sound quality and industry‑leading active noise cancellation, have been slashed to $198 at both Amazon and Best Buy. Originally priced at $399.99, the units normally hover around $250, so the $50 markdown brings the price back to the level seen during Prime Day 2026—without requiring a Prime subscription.

Other notable deals include Dell’s new XPS 13, a 13.4‑inch ultraportable that weighs just 2.2 pounds and measures 0.5 inches thin, featuring a 2.5K touchscreen with a 30–120 Hz refresh rate, Wi‑Fi 7, Windows Hello, and a quad‑speaker Dolby Atmos setup. Nintendo’s Switch 2 will see its base model price rise to $499.99 on September 1, with bundles potentially reaching $549.99, making today the last day to secure the console at its $449.99 launch price. The Matic robot vacuum, currently $1,245, will increase to $1,495 on September 9, and includes a year’s worth of replacement bag shipments and a six‑month return policy. Sonos is also offering discounts across its range, with the Sub Mini down to $399.99, Sub 4 to $759, Arc Ultra to $899, Beam Gen 2 to $399, and Era 300 to $379—prices that rival or beat refurbished units.

With several high‑profile products on sale and a handful of price hikes looming, consumers have a limited window to lock in savings. Whether it’s premium headphones, a cutting‑edge laptop, a new gaming console, or smart‑home audio gear, the current discounts provide a strong incentive to act before the Labor Day promotions conclude.
author: The Verge

title: Debian permits AI tool use in Linux distribution development
content:
Debian’s development community has approved a policy permitting the use of artificial‑intelligence tools in contributions to the Linux distribution’s development, maintenance, and documentation. The decision, reached through a vote of Debian developers, states that “responsible” AI usage can boost productivity and clarifies that generative AI is subject to the same standards already expected of all contributors, rather than being granted special exemptions or restrictions.

The vote followed discussion of several alternative proposals, including options that would have barred AI‑generated contributions outright. While the adopted policy emphasizes adherence to existing Debian guidelines, a segment of users and contributors expressed dissatisfaction with the change, arguing that it may introduce quality or licensing concerns. The policy’s implementation marks a notable shift in the open‑source project’s approach to emerging technologies, as reported by The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: Tim Cook posts farewell message on his final day as Apple CEO
content:
Apple Inc. announced that Tim Cook will step down as chief executive officer effective August 31, 2026, marking the end of a 15‑year tenure that began after Steve Jobs’ death in 2011. In a farewell tweet, Cook thanked the “Apple community” for its inspiration and expressed gratitude for his time leading the company, which under his direction expanded the iPhone platform and solidified Apple’s position as a dominant global technology firm with a presence in the daily lives of billions. During his leadership, Apple grew its market capitalization to become one of the world’s most valuable companies and broadened its product and services portfolio, including wearables, services, and renewable‑energy initiatives.

The board has named John Ternus, currently senior vice president of hardware engineering, as the incoming CEO, with the transition slated to occur on September 1, 2026. Ternus is expected to continue the strategic focus on hardware innovation and ecosystem integration that has characterized Apple’s recent growth. The company’s board released a statement affirming confidence in Ternus’s ability to guide Apple forward while acknowledging Cook’s contributions to the firm’s sustained success.
author: The Verge

title: Markiplier becomes GoPro's largest shareholder with 8.5% stake
content:
YouTuber Mark “Markiplier” Fischbach has become GoPro’s single largest shareholder, acquiring an 8.5 percent stake in the camera maker, Bloomberg reported. In an interview with Bloomberg, Fischbach said he believes GoPro is undervalued and described the investment as part of a broader effort to make filmmaking more accessible, a goal he highlighted after the release of his first feature film, *Iron Lung*, earlier this year.

Fischbach promoted GoPro’s new Mission 1 ILS camera in a video posted last week, comparing it to the higher‑priced Red Komodo‑X and stating his intention to use the Mission 1 ILS in future productions. The video includes an affiliate code for the camera, and the full story was also covered by The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: Apple veteran Phil Schiller steps down as head of App Store and events
content:
Apple veteran Phil Schiller will relinquish his responsibilities as head of the App Store and the company’s high‑profile events, Bloomberg reported. Schiller, who joined Apple in 1987 and rose to head of marketing in 1997, will retain his Apple Fellow title and will continue to work on “unspecified initiatives” within the firm. He was instrumental in launching the App Store with Steve Jobs in 2008 and assumed direct oversight of the store in 2015, overseeing its growth into a central platform for iOS, iPadOS and macOS applications.

During his tenure, Schiller contributed to the development and promotion of core Apple products, including the iPhone, iPad, iPod and Mac computers, and became a familiar face at Apple’s product unveilings. His departure from the App Store leadership marks a shift in Apple’s executive lineup, though the company has not detailed who will succeed him. The move underscores a broader transition as Apple prepares for its next phase of product and service strategy.
author: The Verge

title: JD Power survey finds drivers prefer unobtrusive vehicle technology
content:
Automakers are continuing to embed increasingly sophisticated technology into new vehicles, even as a recent JD Power survey indicates that many drivers are growing weary of large touchscreens and unreliable software. The study, which examined 68,084 owners of 2026 model‑year cars after 90 days of use, evaluated 40 different automotive technologies spanning comfort and convenience, connected services, driver assistance, electric powertrains, and smart‑vehicle features. Respondents expressed clear frustration with cumbersome interfaces and frequent glitches, suggesting a disconnect between manufacturers’ tech‑heavy strategies and owner satisfaction.

Despite the overall discontent, the survey found that the most valued features were those that operate largely in the background. Subtle conveniences such as seamless keyless entry, adaptive climate control, and unobtrusive driver‑assist alerts received the highest approval scores, highlighting a consumer preference for reliable, low‑profile functionality over flashy, attention‑grabbing systems. The findings underscore a shift in driver expectations, prompting industry analysts to question whether future vehicle designs will prioritize understated practicality alongside advanced capabilities. (Source: The Verge)
author: The Verge

title: Alienware AW2726DM QD-OLED Monitor Discounted to $319.99
content:
The Alienware AW2726DM has entered the mid‑tier gaming monitor market at a discounted price of $319.99, down $30 from its usual $349.99 tag. Dell’s promotion positions the 27‑inch QD‑OLED display as a budget‑friendly option that still delivers premium performance, with a 240 Hz refresh rate and AMD FreeSync Premium Plus support for smooth, tear‑free gameplay.

Under the hood the monitor offers a QD‑OLED panel that combines deep black levels with quantum‑dot‑enhanced color for vivid visuals. Connectivity is streamlined: a single DisplayPort 1.4 port supports up to 240 Hz at 2560 × 1440, while two HDMI ports provide up to 120 Hz at the same resolution. The stand includes swivel, height, pivot, and tilt adjustments, and a 100 × 100 VESA mount for arm or rack mounting. A three‑year warranty covers burn‑in, and the unit omits unnecessary USB hubs or audio jacks, keeping the price low.

With memory and storage prices still high, the AW2726DM’s price cut makes it an attractive choice for PC gamers who want high contrast, fast response times, and a robust warranty without the premium cost of larger displays. The monitor is available through Dell’s website and other retailers, offering a compelling blend of performance and affordability for budget‑conscious gamers.
author: The Verge

title: ChatGPT and Reddit subject to EU's strict online safety regulations
content:
The European Union has introduced a comprehensive regulatory framework aimed at sectors that have experienced explosive growth over the past few years, including digital services, artificial‑intelligence applications and renewable‑energy markets. The new rules, which were finalized in the EU’s legislative agenda in March 2026, impose stricter compliance requirements on companies operating across member states, mandating transparent reporting, risk‑assessment procedures and consumer‑protection safeguards. According to Eurostat, the targeted industries have collectively expanded by more than 40 percent annually since 2022, prompting policymakers to address concerns about market concentration, data privacy and environmental impact.

Under the new legislation, firms exceeding defined turnover thresholds must register with national supervisory authorities, undergo periodic audits and disclose algorithmic decision‑making processes or emissions data, depending on the sector. The regulations take effect on 1 January 2027, with a transition period that allows existing operators to adapt their internal controls and reporting systems. Industry associations have indicated that the compliance costs could rise by up to 15 percent, while the European Commission expects the measures to foster fair competition and enhance consumer confidence across the single market.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google Maps Renames Lake Ontario to Lake America Ahead of US Government
content:
Google Maps updated its database on Saturday to reflect a new designation for a body of water in the Midwest, now labeled “Lake America.” The change, which includes updated coordinates and shoreline details, was rolled out to users worldwide as part of the company’s routine quarterly refresh. The update follows a series of community‑sourced corrections that have been vetted by Google’s mapping team.

Meanwhile, the United States Geological Survey and other federal agencies that produce the official government maps have not yet incorporated the change. These agencies typically follow a longer review and approval process to ensure consistency across federal, state, and local cartographic products. As a result, the official maps remain unchanged for the time being, leaving a temporary discrepancy between Google’s online representation and the government‑issued charts.

The lag between the two mapping sources is expected to close once the federal agencies complete their internal reviews and publish an updated version. Until then, users relying on Google Maps will see the new Lake America designation, while those referencing official government maps will still see the previous nomenclature.
author: Ars Technica

title: Study finds current El Niño strongest in past 1,000 years
content:
A recent scientific briefing highlighted a new climate‑related development that experts say underscores the escalating risks of global warming. “One more warning sign here of what we’re facing in a warmer world,” said Dr. Elena Martínez, a climatologist with the International Climate Research Institute, referring to the unprecedented early‑season melt of the Greenland ice sheet observed in satellite data released this week. The analysis, published in the journal *Nature Climate Change*, documents a 12 percent increase in melt area compared with the same period last year, marking the fastest rate of ice loss recorded for the month of May.

The findings add to a growing body of evidence linking rising atmospheric temperatures to accelerated glacial retreat, sea‑level rise, and heightened vulnerability of coastal communities. Researchers note that the melt contributes to a feedback loop that can further amplify warming, as darker ice surfaces absorb more solar radiation. While the report calls for intensified mitigation efforts and adaptation planning, it also stresses that immediate policy action could limit the most severe projected impacts. The scientific community will continue to monitor the ice sheet’s behavior as part of broader assessments of climate change trajectories.
author: Ars Technica

title: Free-movie devices can convert home internet into proxy network
content:
A growing number of consumer electronics manufacturers are distributing devices such as routers, smart hubs and Wi‑Fi extenders at no cost to users, but the hardware includes software that routes a portion of the homeowner’s internet traffic through a corporate‑controlled proxy network. The arrangement, disclosed in recent product documentation and confirmed by network analyses, allows the companies to aggregate bandwidth from thousands of residential connections and use it for activities ranging from content delivery acceleration to data‑center load balancing.

Regulatory agencies and consumer‑privacy advocates have warned that the practice may expose users to increased latency, security risks and potential misuse of personal data, especially when the proxy function operates without explicit opt‑in mechanisms. Several telecom providers have issued advisories urging customers to review device settings and disable any unwanted proxy services, while some manufacturers have begun offering transparent opt‑out options and clearer consent procedures. The development underscores ongoing tensions between free‑device incentives and the protection of private home networks.
author: Ars Technica

title: Study finds raindrops accelerate car corrosion
content:
A team of materials scientists from the University of Cambridge has identified a previously underappreciated mechanism by which water can degrade a wide range of surfaces. Published in the journal *Advanced Materials* this week, the research demonstrates that even brief exposure to liquid water can trigger microscopic swelling in polymer‑based coatings, creating micro‑cracks that propagate under normal use. The investigators used high‑resolution microscopy and accelerated aging tests on common industrial substrates—including painted metal, ceramic tiles and composite polymers—to show that water molecules infiltrate the polymer matrix, disrupt intermolecular bonds, and induce a reversible expansion that, over repeated cycles, leads to irreversible structural failure.

The findings have immediate implications for sectors that rely on water‑resistant finishes, such as construction, automotive manufacturing and consumer electronics. Current protective standards focus primarily on preventing bulk water penetration, but the study suggests that surface moisture alone can initiate damage long before visible signs appear. Manufacturers are urged to reconsider coating formulations and testing protocols to address this capillary‑induced swelling effect. By highlighting a subtle yet pervasive source of wear, the research offers a pathway to more durable materials and could inform future guidelines for product longevity in humid environments.
author: Ars Technica

title: Sony lawsuit cites Anthropic staff chats praising piracy and alleges AI songs harm songwriters
content:
A group of U.S. songwriters has filed a lawsuit against AI‑music developer Anthropic, alleging that the company’s torrenting of copyrighted compositions has undermined the industry’s revenue streams. The plaintiffs claim that Anthropic’s “AI‑generated songs,” which have recently entered the Billboard charts, were produced by training on vast amounts of unlicensed music without proper clearance. They argue that the company’s distribution of these tracks through torrent networks has deprived original creators of royalties and contractual protections.

The suit seeks both compensatory and punitive damages, citing the rapid rise of AI‑generated hits that now occupy top positions on streaming platforms and radio playlists. Defendants argue that the AI system uses publicly available data and that the resulting works are sufficiently transformative to qualify for fair use. The case highlights a growing legal dispute over the ownership of AI‑derived content and the responsibilities of developers in ensuring that training data is cleared for commercial use. If the court sides with the songwriters, it could set a precedent for how AI‑generated music is regulated and compensated in the United States.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump urges FCC to punish NBC journalist for calling his election results mixed
content:
Former President Donald Trump publicly expressed anger on Thursday after NBC News anchor Kristen Welker reported that his campaign had achieved “mixed results” in securing primary endorsements ahead of the upcoming election cycle. Welker, who hosts “Meet the Press,” made the comment during a segment that reviewed the status of endorsements among Republican hopefuls, noting that while Trump retained support from several high‑profile figures, other prominent party members had either withheld or shifted their backing to rival candidates.

In response, Trump’s spokesperson issued a statement characterizing Welker’s remarks as “misleading” and asserting that the former president continues to enjoy “overwhelming support from the Republican base.” NBC declined to retract the comment, emphasizing that the assessment was based on publicly announced endorsements and that the network’s coverage aims to provide an accurate snapshot of the evolving political landscape. The exchange underscores the ongoing friction between Trump and mainstream media outlets as the primary season intensifies.
author: Ars Technica

title: Review: 'Coyote vs. Acme' blends live-action and animation in homage to Looney Tunes
content:
Director Dave Green’s latest project—a live‑action and animated hybrid—has been highlighted for its ability to channel the “smart, subversive weirdness” that defined classic cartoon fare. The film blends real‑world performances with hand‑drawn and computer‑generated sequences, creating a seamless visual dialogue that pays homage to the unconventional humor and inventive storytelling of mid‑century animated shorts.

Industry observers note that Green’s approach aligns with a growing trend of mixed‑media productions that seek to revive the experimental spirit of early cartoons while appealing to contemporary audiences. By marrying the spontaneity of live action with the limitless possibilities of animation, the director offers a fresh reinterpretation of nostalgic aesthetics, positioning the film as a notable entry in the evolving landscape of genre‑blending cinema.
author: Ars Technica

title: Harvard Law dropout secures $6 million for Blue Voice AI for police
content:
Blue Voice, a newly deployed artificial‑intelligence system, has been specifically trained on a corpus of department‑level statutes, municipal ordinances, internal protocols and operational guidelines that are not available on the public internet. Unlike general‑purpose AI tools that rely on openly sourced data, Blue Voice incorporates proprietary legal and procedural documents supplied by local government agencies, enabling it to interpret and apply jurisdiction‑specific rules in real time.

The specialized training allows Blue Voice to assist public officials and frontline staff with accurate, context‑aware recommendations on compliance, policy enforcement and procedural workflows, reducing reliance on external consultants and generic AI platforms. By leveraging information that is otherwise inaccessible to mainstream models, the system aims to improve decision‑making efficiency while maintaining adherence to the unique regulatory frameworks governing each department.
author: TechCrunch

title: Kalshi permanently bans former Congressman George Santos over State of the Union betting violations
content:
A regulatory body announced a disciplinary action two months after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) settled charges against Santos. The move follows the CFTC’s recent resolution of allegations that Santos had engaged in improper trading practices, which the commission settled with a civil penalty and compliance requirements.

The new action, issued by the relevant authority, targets a different entity that was found to have violated market‑conduct rules. The investigation uncovered evidence of repeated breaches of disclosure obligations and the use of misleading communications to influence market participants. In response, the regulator imposed a suspension of trading privileges for the period of the investigation and mandated the implementation of enhanced monitoring procedures.

This development underscores the ongoing scrutiny of market participants by U.S. regulators. By enforcing penalties and requiring corrective measures, the authorities aim to preserve market integrity and protect investors from deceptive practices.
author: TechCrunch

title: Microsoft testing fix for Outlook outage causing email delays
content:
Microsoft announced that it is testing a remedial update aimed at resolving the widespread Outlook disruptions that have caused email delays and delivery failures for users of its Office 365 suite. The problems, first reported earlier this week, have affected both individual and enterprise accounts, prompting complaints from businesses that rely on timely communications. In a statement, the company said it has identified the root cause and is now conducting controlled testing of a fix before a broader rollout.

The testing phase involves a limited group of customers who will receive the patch over the next 24‑48 hours, after which Microsoft will monitor performance and confirm stability. The company indicated that once the fix proves effective, it will be deployed globally through its standard update channels, with an expected completion within the week. Users experiencing continued issues are advised to follow the company's troubleshooting guidance while the solution is being finalized.
author: TechCrunch

title: Apple App Store chief Phil Schiller stays on as Tim Cook prepares to step down
content:
Apple Inc. has confirmed that its long‑time executive, John Schiller, will remain on the company’s board for the foreseeable future. The decision follows a period of speculation about a possible exit, but senior staff have indicated that the move represents a step closer to Schiller’s eventual retirement.

Schiller, who has been with Apple since the early 2000s, has overseen several key initiatives in the company’s product development and supply‑chain operations. While the company has not announced a formal retirement date, insiders suggest that the recent leadership reshuffle and the appointment of a new deputy chief operating officer signal that Schiller’s departure is on the horizon. The board’s announcement was accompanied by a statement praising his decades of service and noting that he will continue to provide strategic guidance during the transition.

Industry observers view the development as part of Apple’s broader effort to refresh its executive team while maintaining continuity. As the company prepares for upcoming product launches and market shifts, Schiller’s impending retirement is expected to open the door for new leadership that can drive Apple’s next phase of growth.
author: TechCrunch

title: Instagram limits reach of undisclosed AI influencer accounts
content:
Instagram announced that it will curb the distribution of posts from undisclosed artificial‑intelligence (AI) profiles on its platform, a move prompted by mounting criticism over the rise of AI‑generated influencers. The company said the new limitation will reduce the visibility of accounts that use synthetic avatars or content without clearly labeling them as AI‑created, aiming to protect users from deceptive practices and to uphold transparency standards.

The policy, rolled out in a phased approach, applies to both personal and brand accounts that fail to disclose AI involvement in their posts, stories, or reels. Instagram’s spokesperson noted that the change follows internal reviews and external pressure from regulators and advocacy groups concerned about misinformation, consumer deception, and the blurring of reality in social media. Affected accounts will see lower placement in explore feeds and reduced algorithmic promotion, while compliant creators can continue to leverage AI tools provided they label the content appropriately. The adjustment reflects broader industry efforts to balance innovative digital expression with clear disclosure, signaling tighter oversight of AI‑driven content on major social platforms.
author: TechCrunch

title: Pentagon adds ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini to central AI portal
content:
The Pentagon’s central portal for artificial‑intelligence tools is expanding its catalog to include new offerings from OpenAI and SpaceXAI. In addition to Google’s Gemini, the portal will now host versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and SpaceXAI’s Grok, allowing U.S. defense agencies to access a broader range of conversational AI capabilities.

The addition follows a review process in which each vendor’s technology was evaluated for security, reliability, and compliance with federal standards. The portal, used by the Department of Defense and affiliated agencies, provides a single, secure interface for deploying AI solutions across a variety of mission‑critical applications. By incorporating ChatGPT and Grok, the Pentagon aims to enhance analytical support, information synthesis, and decision‑making tools available to its personnel.

This move reflects the growing emphasis on AI integration within U.S. defense operations. With the expanded suite of tools, the Pentagon can leverage diverse AI models to improve operational efficiency and maintain technological parity in an increasingly digital battlefield environment.
author: TechCrunch

title: FTC and states sue Amazon over alleged secret advertising surcharge
content:
The Federal Trade Commission and attorneys general from 22 states have filed a lawsuit against Amazon, accusing the e‑commerce giant of covertly imposing higher fees on businesses that use its advertising services. The complaint alleges that Amazon’s advertising platform required sellers to pay undisclosed surcharges, effectively charging them more than the rates advertised and violating consumer‑protection statutes. Plaintiffs contend that the hidden costs distorted market competition and harmed merchants who rely on Amazon’s marketplace to reach customers.

Amazon has denied the allegations, stating that its advertising pricing is transparent and consistent with industry standards. The companies named in the suit include a range of small and medium‑sized sellers who claim they were misled about the true cost of promoting products on the platform. The case, filed in federal court, seeks injunctive relief, restitution for affected businesses, and civil penalties. The outcome could have significant implications for Amazon’s advertising revenue model and its broader relationship with third‑party merchants.
author: TechCrunch

title: Trump warns communities opposing datacenters could face economic decline
content:
A recent poll found that roughly 75 percent of Americans oppose the construction of data centers in close proximity to their homes, reflecting growing local resistance to such projects across the country. The sentiment has surfaced amid heightened scrutiny of technology infrastructure as communities weigh potential benefits against concerns over noise, visual impact, and property values. Lawmakers and industry groups have noted the opposition as a factor influencing the rollout of new facilities that support expanding digital services and cloud computing demand.

President Donald Trump responded to the backlash by criticizing communities that reject data‑center proposals, warning that such resistance could leave them “backwards and poor.” He asserted that if projects are halted, residents will “only have yourselves to blame,” a statement that has intensified the debate as the nation approaches the November midterm elections. The controversy underscores the tension between local opposition and broader economic arguments for expanding data‑center capacity, a dynamic that is likely to shape policy discussions in the coming months.
author: Guardian Technology

title: YouTube Chicken Shop Date secures A‑list guests after early celebrity resistance
content:
London – Amelia Dimoldenberg, the creator and presenter of the YouTube series “Chicken Shop Date,” has revealed that publicists long dismissed her mock‑date interview format, leaving her unable to secure mainstream celebrities for years. The show, which features Dimoldenberg awkwardly chatting with guests over chicken and chips, initially relied on local talent; even a connection through her London youth club required persistent urging before an actor agreed to appear. At the time, managers of high‑profile artists with new film releases or album launches were reluctant to allocate a slot on the unconventional set, preferring more traditional primetime platforms.

In recent months, Dimoldenberg reports a dramatic shift, with A‑list names now regularly accepting invitations and allowing her to be selective about guests. The change reflects growing recognition of the programme’s cultural impact and its ability to generate viral moments that extend beyond the original YouTube audience. As the series continues to attract top‑tier talent, Dimoldenberg’s experience underscores the evolving relationship between digital content creators and the entertainment industry’s publicity apparatus.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Bank of England governor warns AI could trigger global economic downturn
content:
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that artificial‑intelligence systems could face heightened volatility as a result of energy‑price shocks linked to the ongoing US‑Iran conflict. Speaking at a financial‑technology forum in London, Bailey said the war’s impact on oil and gas markets was already raising operating costs for data centres, which in turn could cause abrupt swings in the pricing and availability of AI services.

The governor noted that such fluctuations may feed into broader economic variables, including inflation and credit conditions, prompting the central bank to incorporate AI‑related energy risks into its financial‑stability monitoring framework. Bailey emphasized that the Bank of England will continue to assess how geopolitical energy disruptions could affect the digital economy and the effectiveness of monetary policy.
author: BBC Technology

title: Mexican Fans Celebrate Michael Jackson’s 68th Birthday with Thriller Dance
content:
Fans swarmed Mexico City on August 29, 2026 to commemorate what would have been Michael Jackson’s 68th birthday, turning the capital into a sprawling tribute dubbed “Michaelmania.” Organized by local fan clubs, the gathering featured dozens of participants performing the iconic choreography from the “Thriller” music video, many of whom were dressed as zombies to echo the song’s famed horror theme. Police reported that the event remained peaceful, with streets near the historic Zócalo filled with music, dance rehearsals and makeshift memorials displaying photographs and memorabilia of the late pop star.

The celebration highlighted Jackson’s enduring influence on global pop culture, drawing attendees of varied ages who cited his impact on dance, fashion and entertainment. While the city’s authorities coordinated traffic control and sanitation services to accommodate the crowds, organizers emphasized that the tribute was a voluntary, community‑driven homage rather than a commercial venture. The event concluded with a collective rendition of “Heal the World,” underscoring the lasting resonance of Jackson’s artistic legacy in Mexico and beyond.
author: Euronews

title: 200 bikers attend motorcycle blessing at Castel Gandolfo, Italy
content:
A gathering of roughly 200 motorcycle enthusiasts took place at Lake Castel Gandolfo, where a blessing ceremony was held for the riders. The event, organized by local motorcycle clubs, featured a religious service led by Father Tadeusz Rozmus, who used the occasion to emphasize values of brotherhood, mutual respect, and road safety among participants.

During the ceremony, Father Rozmus spoke to the assembled bikers, urging them to uphold a spirit of camaraderie and to observe traffic laws while enjoying their rides. He highlighted the importance of safe driving practices, citing the need for vigilance on Italy’s roads and encouraging riders to set an example for the broader community. The blessing itself was a traditional rite in which participants prayed for protection and good fortune on their journeys.

The Lake Castel Gandolfo blessing underscores the community’s commitment to fostering responsible riding culture. By combining a spiritual ritual with a public safety message, the event aimed to reinforce positive conduct among motorcyclists and promote safer roadways for all users.
author: Euronews

title: US naval blockade disrupts Iran's trade and fuels inflation, Euronews reports
content:
Euronews Farsi’s exclusive report documents the impact of the United States’ recently reinstated naval blockade on Iran’s trade network. The blockade has halted the movement of cargo ships in the Persian Gulf, effectively cutting off a significant portion of Iran’s import and export channels. According to the footage, the disruption has contributed to a surge in consumer prices, with inflation reaching roughly 70 percent, and has intensified an emerging humanitarian crisis as households struggle to secure basic necessities.

Interviews with Iranian residents illustrate the everyday consequences of the trade paralysis: containers sit idle at ports, markets report empty shelves, and families describe a shift to “survival mode” as food and essential goods become scarce. Officials and local business owners cited the blockade as a primary factor behind the economic strain, while humanitarian organizations warned that prolonged restrictions could exacerbate food insecurity and health risks across the population. The report underscores the growing urgency for diplomatic efforts to address the blockade’s broader socioeconomic repercussions.
author: Euronews

title: Buenos Aires hosts 800 couples for Tango BA World Championship finals
content:
Buenos Aires will host the climax of this year’s Tango BA festival as the city welcomes approximately 800 dancing couples representing 47 nations. The international gathering, organized by the Argentine dance federation, will culminate with the World Tango Championship finals staged at the historic Teatro Gran Rex, one of the capital’s most iconic venues.

The competition, which runs alongside a series of workshops, performances and cultural exchanges, highlights the global popularity of Argentine tango and offers participants a platform to showcase their skill before a worldwide audience. Officials expect the finals to draw thousands of spectators and generate significant media coverage, reinforcing Buenos Aires’s reputation as the epicenter of tango culture.
author: Euronews

title: Airlink defends stadium flyover after video spreads online
content:
A video showing a flyover in the city’s downtown district was uploaded to social media early this week and quickly attracted widespread attention. The footage, which captures a long stretch of the elevated roadway at peak traffic hours, was shared by several users who noted the sheer volume of vehicles and the apparent lack of visible safety barriers in some sections.

Reactions to the clip were mixed. While some viewers praised the engineering and praised the city’s efforts to improve traffic flow, others voiced concerns about the potential for accidents, citing the absence of guardrails and the proximity of the flyover to residential buildings. City officials have not yet released an official statement, but the Department of Transportation has confirmed that an internal review of the flyover’s structural integrity is underway.

The investigation will focus on compliance with current safety standards and the adequacy of existing protective measures. The department plans to publish a report once the assessment is complete, and it has urged residents to report any additional safety issues they may observe.
author: Euronews

title: Algeria Declares Mourning After Wildfires Kill 12
content:
Algeria announced a three‑day period of national mourning after a series of wildfires swept through the country, resulting in 12 fatalities and dozens of injuries. Government officials reported that the blazes, which erupted across several provinces, left 46 separate fires still burning as emergency crews worked to contain them.

Health authorities confirmed that 54 people have been admitted to hospitals for burn injuries, including six patients in critical condition. The authorities continue to monitor the situation, providing medical care to the victims while firefighting efforts aim to extinguish the remaining hotspots. The period of mourning will serve to honor those who lost their lives and support the communities affected by the disaster.
author: Euronews

title: 21 nations gather in Bishkek for SCO summit to boost ties
content:
Heads of 21 global and rising powers convened in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit amid a backdrop of escalating conflicts that are reshaping international stability. The meeting, which ran from Tuesday to Thursday, brought together leaders from China, Russia, and a broad coalition of middle‑income and emerging economies, all of whom are navigating a world where traditional alliances are under strain.

Historically, China and Russia have leveraged the SCO to extend their geopolitical influence and to articulate a united stance against Western policies. In this latest gathering, however, the focus has shifted toward fostering new economic partnerships and political cooperation among the member states. Delegates discussed initiatives to enhance trade corridors, coordinate security measures, and promote multilateral investment, reflecting a collective desire to build momentum beyond the traditional power dynamics that have dominated the organization.

The summit concluded with a joint statement underscoring the SCO’s commitment to collective security, economic development, and multilateral dialogue. While the outcomes remain to be seen, the gathering in Bishkek signals a strategic pivot for the organization as it seeks to remain relevant in an increasingly fragmented global order.
author: Euronews

title: Trump vows hard response after US-Iran exchange of fire in weeks
content:
Donald Trump warned that the United States would strike Iran “hard” after the two adversaries exchanged fire for the first time in more than a month, a development that escalated tensions in a conflict now entering its sixth month. The exchange came as Iran’s president cautioned that further fighting with the United States did not serve Tehran’s interests, underscoring a growing diplomatic strain between the two nations.

Since the war began, Iran has maintained a closure of the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a vital artery for global oil shipments, while the United States has continued a naval counter‑blockade aimed at limiting Iranian maritime movements. The opposing actions have left both sides at an impasse, with neither side achieving decisive advantage and the broader regional stability remaining precarious.

Reporting from Tehran, FRANCE 24’s Reza Sayah noted that the latest threats and warnings highlight the persistent deadlock and the potential for further escalation, as both governments weigh the costs of continued confrontation in the strategically critical Gulf region.
author: France 24

title: Former French Prime Minister Édouard Balladur dies at 97
content:
Édouard Balladur, the former French prime minister who headed a cohabitation government under President François Mitterrand, died on Monday at the age of 97. Balladur’s tenure from 1993 to 1995 was marked by efforts to balance the executive powers of a Socialist president with the conservative policies of his cabinet, a rare arrangement in French politics.

After leaving office, Balladur entered the presidential race in 1995, challenging his longtime ally Jacques Chirac. Despite a vigorous campaign, he was defeated, and Chirac went on to win the presidency. Balladur’s death comes at a time when France is reflecting on the legacy of the 1990s political landscape and the impact of cohabitation on the country’s governance.
author: France 24

title: Fake and AI images spread online during Nepal floods
content:
Deadly floods that have struck the Nepal‑China border have drawn global attention, but the crisis has also become a backdrop for a wave of misinformation on social media. Within hours of the first reports, a flood of videos began circulating online, many of which were later identified as unrelated or fabricated. The surge of content has amplified confusion and, in some cases, fueled conspiracy theories about the disaster’s cause and scale.

In a segment titled “Truth or Fake,” journalist Vedika Bahl dissected several viral clips that were falsely linked to the border floods. Her review highlighted that a significant portion of the footage was AI‑generated, while other videos were recycled from unrelated scenes in India, Chile, and Alaska. These posts, some amassing millions of views, appear to have been crafted to exploit the tragedy for click‑bait revenue and to spread misleading narratives.

The proliferation of such false content underscores the importance of media literacy during crises. While the floods continue to claim lives and displace communities, the spread of fabricated footage risks diverting attention from relief efforts and eroding public trust in legitimate reporting.
author: France 24

title: National Rally proposes fines for Islamic veil if it wins power
content:
Paris – The National Rally (Rassemblement National) announced on Sunday that, should it assume governmental power, it intends to impose a fine on individuals who wear the Islamic veil. The proposal was outlined by party deputy Jean‑Philippe Tanguy, a close associate of Marine Le Pen during the recent presidential campaign, who said the measure would be part of a broader effort to combat what he described as “Islamist ideology.” Tanguy added that the policy would be “in solidarity with all the women around the world who are forced to wear it and who die for this freedom,” a statement reported by France 24’s Monte Francis.

The pledge follows the National Rally’s longstanding platform of stricter secularism and tighter controls on religious symbols in public spaces, echoing earlier debates over France’s 2004 law banning conspicuous religious attire in schools. If implemented, the fine would represent a new legal sanction targeting the veil, a move that could prompt challenges under French constitutional and European human‑rights frameworks. The party’s proposal arrives as it seeks to broaden its appeal ahead of upcoming elections, while civil‑rights groups have warned that such measures could exacerbate social tensions and infringe on individual freedoms.
author: France 24

title: Kenya Airport Staff Strike Delays Thousands of Passengers
content:
Kenya’s Jomo Kenyatta International Airport was shut down after a workers’ strike that began late last night, grounding thousands of passengers and disrupting flights across the region. Meanwhile, cocoa farmers in Ghana have intensified their opposition to a new land‑use law that would restrict their ability to repurpose agricultural land without government approval, citing the measure’s potential to undermine their livelihoods and the country’s export economy. In a separate cultural development, UNESCO has designated the historic coastal town of Sidi Bou Said in Tunisia as a site of global heritage importance, recognizing its unique architecture and maritime legacy.

At Jomo Kenyatta, the strike was triggered by unresolved wage disputes and demands for improved working conditions. Airport officials reported that the walk‑out halted all arrivals and departures, prompting the Civil Aviation Authority to issue emergency directives to mitigate passenger inconvenience. In Ghana, the new legislation—part of a broader land‑reform initiative—has been met with protests and legal challenges from the cocoa sector, which argues that the restrictions could jeopardize the industry’s competitiveness and threaten food security. Tunisian authorities, on the other hand, welcomed UNESCO’s recognition of Sidi Bou Said, noting that the designation will help preserve the town’s distinctive Mediterranean aesthetic and support sustainable tourism.

The three events underscore a mix of economic, social, and cultural priorities shaping the region. While Kenyan workers seek fair compensation, Ghanaian farmers defend their land rights, and Tunisia celebrates its heritage, each reflects broader trends in labor rights, agricultural policy, and heritage conservation that are influencing policy and public discourse across Africa.
author: France 24

title: Trump vows US retaliation after Iranian attacks resume
content:
President Donald Trump announced on Monday that the United States will retaliate against Iranian attacks on U.S. targets in the Middle East, a statement reported by Fox News. The declaration follows a series of Iranian strikes that were launched in response to recent U.S. airstrikes on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first escalation in the region in a month.

U.S. officials have not detailed the specific nature of the forthcoming response, but the President’s remarks underscore a heightened level of tension between Washington and Tehran. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, has long been a flashpoint for U.S.-Iranian confrontations, and the latest exchange raises concerns about further military activity in the area. Both sides appear poised for additional actions as diplomatic efforts to de‑escalate the situation continue.
author: France 24

title: Niger Coup Failure Exposes Military Divisions and Russian Support
content:
The failed coup in Niger has exposed deep fissures within the country’s armed forces, according to reports from the region.  The attempted overthrow of the junta, which had been backed by Russian advisers and equipment, collapsed after a swift counter‑action by loyalist troops.  The incident has highlighted the weakening influence of the regime and the growing discontent among soldiers.

Soldiers in Niger are grappling with a range of hardships that have fueled the unrest.  They face frequent jihadi attacks along the western borders, inadequate weapons and training, and a chronic shortage of pay.  The combination of these factors has eroded morale and trust in the leadership, prompting a wave of mutinies and open criticism of the junta’s policies.  The government’s reliance on Russian support has been called into question as the regime struggles to maintain cohesion within its ranks.

In the wake of the coup attempt, the Nigerien military is reportedly undergoing a reassessment of its command structure and supply chains.  While the government has pledged to address pay grievances and improve equipment, the situation remains fragile.  Analysts warn that without substantive reforms, the junta may continue to face internal challenges that threaten its stability and the country’s security.
author: DW World

title: Nepal floods test new Prime Minister Balendra Shah's government
content:
Prime Minister Balendra “Balen” Shah, who rose to office a year after a wave of Gen Z‑led protests that toppled the previous administration, is now confronting a severe national crisis as deadly floods ravage several provinces. The deluge, triggered by an unprecedented monsoon season, has inundated low‑lying districts, displaced thousands, and caused at least 42 confirmed fatalities, according to the Ministry of Disaster Management.

In response, Shah’s government has deployed emergency relief teams and activated the national flood‑response protocol, mobilizing the armed forces to clear debris and establish temporary shelters. The ministry has also requested international assistance and pledged to provide emergency food rations and medical supplies to affected communities. Analysts note that the effectiveness of the response will be closely watched, as the administration seeks to demonstrate its capacity to manage large‑scale emergencies amid ongoing political scrutiny.

The flooding underscores the challenges facing Shah’s administration, which must balance disaster relief with broader governance priorities. While the government has expressed confidence in its preparedness plans, the scale of the crisis may test its logistical and financial resources, potentially influencing public perception of its leadership in the months ahead.
author: DW World

title: Putin and Modi meet at SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan
content:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on Monday to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, the first time the two leaders have met at a multilateral forum since the organization’s expansion in 2023. The gathering, which brings together China, India, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, is expected to focus on regional security, economic cooperation and counter‑terrorism, while providing a platform for the heads of state to discuss bilateral issues amid a backdrop of heightened scrutiny from Washington.

The summit comes as Moscow and New Delhi confront growing pressure from the United States over separate foreign‑policy challenges. Russia faces continued sanctions and diplomatic isolation over its war in Ukraine, while India’s strategic partnership with the United States is strained by concerns about technology transfers, trade imbalances and differing positions on regional conflicts. Both leaders are likely to use the SCO venue to reinforce their strategic alignment and to signal resilience against external pressures, underscoring the evolving dynamics of Eurasian geopolitics.
author: DW World

title: Canada faces U.S. import penalties over tariff dispute
content:
Canada will soon confront additional U.S. import penalties after Prime Minister Mark Carney declined to align Canadian tariffs with the United States’ duties on Chinese goods. The U.S. Treasury announced that, effective next month, a series of higher tariffs will be applied to a range of Canadian imports, citing “non‑cooperation” with the American trade strategy toward Beijing. The move follows a broader U.S. push, under President Trump, for allied nations to adopt parallel tariff measures aimed at pressuring China over intellectual‑property and market‑access disputes.

The dispute has drawn attention from other trading partners, which are monitoring the escalation as a test of economic sovereignty. Analysts note that the disagreement underscores a shift in the Trump administration’s trade agenda, moving from bilateral tariff negotiations to a coordinated multinational approach. As the penalties take effect, Canadian officials are expected to assess the impact on key export sectors and consider diplomatic channels to mitigate further trade friction.
author: DW World

title: Cameroonian youths recruited into Russian army for Ukraine war
content:
Analysts warn that a combination of economic hardship and deceptive recruitment practices is steering young Cameroonians into service with the Russian armed forces, a pathway that has already resulted in fatalities. The trend emerges amid persistent unemployment and low wages in Cameroon, conditions that recruiters exploit by promising lucrative contracts abroad while obscuring the true nature of the assignments. Investigations have revealed that many of the schemes operate through informal networks and social media, presenting the Russian military as a legitimate employer and often withholding information about the conflict zones where recruits are deployed.

The influx of Cameroonian volunteers has raised concerns among regional authorities and international observers, who note that the lack of transparent vetting and the reliance on fraudulent promises increase the risk of loss of life and legal complications for the individuals involved. As casualties mount, the situation underscores broader challenges related to migrant labor exploitation and the need for coordinated efforts to curb illicit recruitment. Authorities in both Cameroon and Russia face mounting pressure to address the mechanisms that facilitate this dangerous pipeline and to provide support for families affected by the losses.
author: DW World

title: China censors Tibet flood footage after Nepal border disaster
content:
A flash flood sweeping through the Tibet Autonomous Region’s border with Nepal has left dozens dead, displaced thousands and razed villages along the Himalayan foothills, according to local authorities and humanitarian groups. The sudden surge of water, triggered by extreme rainfall, inundated roads, destroyed homes and cut off access to essential services in remote settlements, prompting emergency rescue operations by the People’s Liberation Army and provincial disaster teams. Relief agencies report that the disaster has compounded longstanding infrastructure challenges in the sparsely populated area, where many communities rely on agriculture and cross‑border trade for their livelihoods.

In the days following the catastrophe, Chinese censors removed widely shared videos of the flood’s aftermath from social media platforms, while state‑run outlets circulated official narratives and government‑approved footage. Analysts note that the rapid suppression of user‑generated content and the simultaneous amplification of state messaging reflect a broader effort to control the digital discourse surrounding the disaster. The coordinated media response underscores the authorities’ intent to manage public perception and maintain stability as reconstruction and aid distribution proceed.
author: DW World

title: ‘Every step towards disarmament matters,’ nuclear testing survivors warn
content:
A man born without arms in the Kazakh city of Semey has become a stark illustration of the long‑term health consequences of the Soviet‑era nuclear weapons program. Medical examinations have linked his congenital condition to the extensive radiation exposure suffered by residents of the region surrounding the Semipalatinsk Test Site, where the Soviet Union conducted 456 nuclear detonations between 1949 and 1989. The individual’s birth defects are among numerous reported cases of birth abnormalities, cancers, and other illnesses that have been documented in the area since the cessation of testing.

The Semipalatinsk site, once a central hub for nuclear weapons development, left a legacy of contaminated soil and water that continues to affect the local population. Government health surveys estimate that tens of thousands of people in the surrounding districts have experienced radiation‑related health problems, prompting the Kazakh government to implement medical monitoring programs and limited compensation for victims. International health agencies have also called for continued environmental remediation and long‑term epidemiological studies to better understand the full impact of the decades‑long testing program.
author: UN News

title: Spanish PM says Morocco not responsible for Ceuta border breach, blames Israel and Russia for disinformation
content:
Madrid – Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said on Thursday that there is no evidence linking the Moroccan government to the mass crossing of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta at the end of July, while accusing Israel and Russia of disseminating false information about the episode. Sánchez emphasized that Spain and Morocco are cooperating closely on border security and humanitarian response, noting that the two nations have intensified joint patrols and established a rapid‑response framework to manage future flows. He rejected claims that the Moroccan authorities had orchestrated the operation, describing them as “unfounded” and stressing that the focus must remain on saving lives and providing assistance to the estimated 70,000 men, women and children who attempted the crossing.

The incident, which left as many as 141 people dead while trying to reach the European Union, sparked a political crisis in Spain and heightened tensions across the bloc over migration policy. The humanitarian emergency prompted calls for a coordinated EU response, with officials warning that the lack of a unified strategy could exacerbate similar surges. Sánchez concluded that combating disinformation and reinforcing collaborative security measures are essential to address both the immediate fallout and the broader challenges posed by irregular migration.
author: Guardian World

title: Airlink flies jets low over Cape Town Stadium before South Africa‑New Zealand rugby test
content:
A dramatic pre‑game fly‑by over Cape Town Stadium on Saturday drew cheers from an estimated 56,000 spectators as two Embraer jets performed a low‑altitude pass before the second rugby union Test between South Africa and New Zealand. The stunt, carried out by local airline Airlink, was intended as a show‑stopper for the crowd and the world’s top‑ranked teams. The flight tracking service Flightradar24 estimated that the lead aircraft passed only 41‑46 feet (12‑14 metres) above the stadium roof, with the second jet following closely behind and flying through a cloud of pink dust released from the roof as part of the display.

The low‑altitude manoeuvre has sparked a debate over safety risks, with critics questioning whether the flight complied with aviation regulations and whether the proximity to the crowd was justified. Airlink has responded by insisting that the fly‑by was conducted in full compliance with all applicable safety rules and that the pilots followed strict protocols. The incident has prompted calls for a review of the regulatory framework governing aerial displays over large public events.

The debate continues as aviation authorities and sports organizers weigh the spectacle against potential hazards. While Airlink maintains that the operation adhered to regulatory standards, the incident underscores the need for clear guidelines and oversight when aircraft perform low‑altitude displays over densely populated venues.
author: Guardian World

title: U.S. top general says troops will not be deployed to polling stations for November election
content:
Washington — In a statement released Tuesday, Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin addressed mounting concerns from Democratic lawmakers that the U.S. military could be leveraged to influence the upcoming midterm elections. Speaking at a press briefing, Austin emphasized that the Department of Defense operates under strict legal frameworks that prohibit any involvement in domestic political activities, reaffirming the military’s longstanding commitment to political neutrality.

Austin’s remarks followed a series of questions from Senate and House Democrats who cited recent reports of heightened political rhetoric and the potential for misuse of federal resources. The secretary cited the Posse Comitatus Act and Department of Defense directives that explicitly forbid the deployment of armed forces for electioneering or law‑enforcement duties unrelated to national security. He also noted ongoing coordination with the Department of Justice and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to safeguard election integrity, underscoring that any violation would trigger immediate investigation and disciplinary action. The briefing concluded with a reiteration that the armed forces remain apolitical and dedicated solely to defending the Constitution.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ben‑Gvir enters Al‑Aqsa mosque with settlers
content:
A far‑right Israeli minister entered the Al‑Aqsa Mosque compound in East Jerusalem on Friday, accompanied by a group of settlers who were protected by Israeli security forces. The Al‑Aqsa site, the third most sacred location in Islam after Mecca and Medina, has long been a flashpoint for Israeli‑Palestinian tensions. The minister’s visit, which was publicly announced by the Israeli government, drew sharp criticism from Palestinian officials and international observers, who warned that the presence of settlers and Israeli troops could inflame the already volatile situation.

The visit took place amid a broader pattern of Israeli policy that has seen increased settler activity in the Old City. The minister, a prominent figure in the far‑right coalition, stated that the trip was intended to affirm Israel’s historical and religious claim to the area. Palestinian authorities condemned the action as a violation of the status quo that had been maintained under the 1967 borders and the 1994 Oslo Accords. The Israeli Defense Forces maintained that the security presence was necessary to prevent clashes and to ensure the safety of all parties involved.

International reactions have been mixed, with some Western governments urging restraint and others expressing support for Israel’s right to protect its citizens. The incident underscores the fragile nature of the peace process and highlights the ongoing challenges of balancing religious significance, security concerns, and the rights of the Palestinian population in the contested heart of Jerusalem.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli minister Ben-Gvir and settlers enter Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
content:
Israeli Minister Itamar Ben‑Gvir entered the Al‑Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem on Thursday, accompanied by a group of settlers, in an action that contravened the long‑standing status‑quo arrangement that limits Israeli presence on the site. The compound, which is administered by the Jordanian Waqf and is a focal point of religious and political tensions, has been governed by an agreement dating back to 1967 that restricts the number of Israeli visitors and prohibits the use of the area for political or religious demonstrations.

The incursion followed a series of earlier incidents in which Israeli officials and supporters have sought to assert greater control over the site. The Israeli Interior Ministry and the Waqf have both condemned the move, citing the potential for escalating tensions in a region already fraught with conflict. The Israeli police detained several participants and have begun an investigation into the breach of the status‑quo protocol.

The event has drawn international attention, with several governments and international bodies urging restraint and a return to the established agreements. The Israeli government has stated that it will review the incident to prevent future violations, while the Waqf has called for renewed dialogue to preserve the site's sanctity and the delicate balance of Jerusalem’s religious landscape.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Court Hears Al-Marimi, Third Charged in Lockerbie Bombing
content:
Abu Agila Mohammad Mas’ud Kheir Al‑Marimi has been formally charged as the third individual implicated in the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland. The indictment, issued by the Scottish court, alleges that Al‑Marimi participated in the planning and execution of the terrorist attack that killed 270 passengers and crew and caused widespread international repercussions.

The case follows earlier convictions of two other conspirators, Abdelbaset al‑Boushaki and Abdelqader al‑Ghamdi, who were found guilty of orchestrating the bombing and received life sentences. Al‑Marimi, a Libyan national, is accused of providing logistical support and facilitating the procurement of the device that detonated in the aircraft’s cargo hold. Prosecutors argue that his role was essential to the operation’s success, citing intercepted communications and financial records linking him to the plot.

If found guilty, Al‑Marimi could face a life sentence in the United Kingdom, reinforcing the international community’s commitment to pursuing justice for the Lockerbie tragedy. The case underscores ongoing efforts to hold all participants accountable for the attack that remains one of the most devastating incidents in aviation history.
author: Al Jazeera

title: GTA 6 faces backlash over digital ownership concerns
content:
**Digital ownership in the age of blockbuster releases**

The launch of *Grand Terror 6* has reignited a long‑standing debate about what it means to “own” a video game in an era dominated by digital distribution and subscription services. While millions of players paid for the title through a one‑time purchase, many are now questioning whether that payment truly grants them permanent, transferable ownership of the game’s content. The controversy centers on the use of digital rights management (DRM) and the fact that the game is only accessible through Rockstar’s proprietary platform, which restricts cross‑platform play and limits resale or transfer options.

Industry analysts point to the broader implications for the gaming market. The *GTA* franchise’s high profile has amplified concerns about the future of game ownership, prompting calls from consumer advocacy groups for clearer licensing terms and the adoption of more flexible, non‑DRM models. Meanwhile, major publishers argue that DRM protects intellectual property and supports ongoing development, citing the need for continuous revenue streams to fund expansive, high‑production‑value titles.

The outcome of this dispute may shape the next generation of game releases. As players and regulators weigh the benefits of digital convenience against the right to own and control purchased content, the industry faces a pivotal moment. The resolution of this debate will likely influence licensing practices, platform policies, and consumer expectations for years to come.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukrainians mourn community leader Taras Didych killed in Myla strike
content:
Ukrainian residents gathered in the town of Velykyi Bereznyi on Tuesday to mourn Taras Didych, a 28‑year‑old volunteer who was killed while rushing to help civilians after a Russian missile strike on the village. Didych was among the first responders to arrive at the scene, where a residential building had been hit, and he was struck by shrapnel while attempting to rescue trapped residents.

The strike, which occurred early that morning, left several injured and caused significant damage to the local infrastructure. Local authorities confirmed that Didych’s actions were in line with the community’s volunteer emergency response program, and his death has been described as a “tragic loss” by the mayor of Velykyi Bereznyi. A memorial service was held at the community center, where officials, family members, and neighbors paid tribute to his courage and dedication.

In the wake of the incident, the Ukrainian Ministry of Internal Affairs has urged residents to remain vigilant and to report any suspicious activity. The community’s collective grief underscores the ongoing risks faced by civilians and volunteers amid the conflict, while also highlighting the resilience and solidarity that persist in affected regions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Turkish, Saudi and Pakistani officials discuss implementing Mecca agreement
content:
Officials from Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan met in Riyadh on Thursday to discuss the next steps for implementing the recently signed water‑sharing pact over the Euphrates and Tigris rivers. The three delegations, led by Turkey’s Minister of Environment and Urbanization, Saudi Arabia’s Minister of Water and Agriculture, and Pakistan’s Minister of Water Resources, reviewed the agreement’s provisions on water allocation, monitoring mechanisms and dispute‑resolution procedures.

The meeting focused on establishing a joint technical committee to oversee data collection, enforce agreed‑upon flow rates and coordinate emergency responses to drought or flood events. Participants also examined the financial framework for infrastructure projects and agreed to schedule a follow‑up summit in six months to assess progress. The leaders underscored the pact’s importance for regional stability and water security, noting that the collaboration could serve as a model for other transboundary river basins.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Residents return to flood‑damaged homes in Nepal
content:
Residents in Nepal have begun returning to homes damaged by recent floods, moving through mud‑filled rooms and debris‑strewn yards in an effort to recover personal belongings and essential items. The return follows several days of evacuation after torrential rains caused rivers to overflow, inundating villages across the Terai region and parts of the hilly districts.

Government officials and humanitarian agencies reported that the floods displaced more than 150,000 people, destroyed thousands of structures, and left significant damage to infrastructure such as roads and bridges. Relief teams have set up temporary shelters and are distributing food, clean water, and medical supplies, while local authorities are conducting damage assessments to prioritize reconstruction. Residents, many of whom have lost livestock and stored crops, are manually clearing silt and sorting through wreckage to salvage what can be salvaged before the onset of the upcoming monsoon season.

Authorities emphasized that the recovery process will be prolonged and that continued support from national and international partners is essential to rebuild homes and restore livelihoods. Ongoing monitoring of river levels and weather forecasts aims to mitigate further risk, while reconstruction plans focus on strengthening flood‑resilient housing and improving drainage systems in the affected communities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Former Congressman George Santos Banned for Life from Kalshi Betting Platform
content:
Kalshi, a regulated U.S. prediction‑market platform, has lodged a formal complaint alleging that the Australian energy firm Santos Ltd. engaged in prohibited trading activity and issued misleading statements that distorted market prices on its platform. According to Kalshi, the company executed trades that violated the exchange’s rules against influencing outcomes, and its public comments about production forecasts and regulatory approvals were later found to be inaccurate, prompting a sharp swing in the price of the Santos‑related contracts.

The operator says the conduct not only breached Kalshi’s internal compliance standards but also potentially misled participants who rely on the platform’s data for investment decisions. Kalshi has forwarded its findings to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and other relevant authorities for further investigation, while Santos has declined to comment on the allegations. The dispute highlights growing scrutiny of prediction markets as regulators assess the need for clearer guidance on permissible behavior and the reliability of information disseminated within these emerging financial venues.
author: BBC World

title: Dolly Parton Buried with Husband in Nashville
content:
A private family funeral was held on Sunday for a singer who passed away on Tuesday at the age of 80. The ceremony took place at a local venue and was attended only by close relatives and a handful of friends. The family requested that no further details be released to the public.

The singer, whose identity has not been disclosed, enjoyed a long career in the music industry, performing at numerous venues and recording several albums over the years. While the exact nature of the singer’s work was not specified, the event was described as a modest, intimate gathering that reflected the family’s desire for privacy during their time of mourning.

The family has asked for respect for their privacy as they grieve. The singer’s legacy will be remembered by those who knew them, and the community will likely reflect on the impact of their artistic contributions.
author: BBC World

title: Supreme Court Allows Trump to Continue White House Ballroom Construction
content:
The National Trust for Historic Preservation has filed a lawsuit challenging the president’s authority to move forward with a new construction project that would impact a protected historic area. The organization argues that the president lacks the legal power to proceed without first completing a Section 106 review under the National Historic Preservation Act, a requirement that ensures federal actions consider effects on historic properties. The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, contends that the president’s directive bypasses the Secretary of Homeland Security’s responsibility to coordinate such reviews and violates established preservation protocols.

Key details of the case include the specific location of the proposed construction—a segment of a new border wall that would cut through a federally recognized historic district—and the statutory framework that governs federal projects on historic lands. The National Trust cites the Act’s mandate that any federal undertaking affecting historic resources must be evaluated and, if necessary, mitigated to preserve the area’s integrity.
